    level="1"
    right="Feat 11"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[A Home in Every Port](/Feats.aspx?ID=2105) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Downtime" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=49" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 202

**Prerequisites**
Charisma 16

</column>

---

You have a reputation in towns and villages you've visited, and residents are always willing to open their doors to you. When in a town or village, during downtime, you can spend 8 hours to locate a resident willing to provide lodging for you and up to six allies for up to 24 hours at no charge. [The standard of living within the acquired lodging is comfortable, and square meals are provided at no cost](/Equipment.aspx?Category=2). After 24 hours, you must pay standard prices for further lodging and meals or use this feat again to find a new resident willing to host you.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[A Hush Falls Over the World](/Feats.aspx?ID=9383) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Illusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=92" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 107

**Archetype** [World Rouser](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=396)

**Prerequisites**
[World Rouser Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9376)

**Requirements**
Your waking world is active.

</column>

---

Sound is absorbed in your waking world, covering everything in a shroud of quiet until the start of your next turn. Creatures in your waking world become hidden to [imprecise hearing](/Rules.aspx?ID=2407) or [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) to [precise hearing](/Rules.aspx?ID=2406). A creature in your waking world attempting to use spell or effect with the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) or [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) trait must succeed at a DC 4 [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333); on a failure, the spell or effect is [disrupted](/Rules.aspx?ID=2236). Anytime a creature in the area is affected by an auditory or sonic effect, they must attempt a DC 16 flat check. On a success, they are not affected by the auditory or sonic effect, though they still may be affected by other aspects of an ability (for example, a creature hit by a weapon with a [_thundering_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2850) rune would not take sonic damage but would still take the normal damage from the weapon).

**Source** [Foolish Housekeeping and Other Articles](/Sources.aspx?ID=239) **Archetype** [Venture-Gossip](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=311) **Prerequisites** [Venture-Gossip Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7599) --- _Nethys Note: This is a part of the April Fool's content from Paizo's blogs._ You transform into a small bird, such as a finch or a sparrow, allowing you to eavesdrop on others and gain information you wouldn’t otherwise be able to acquire. You become Tiny, gain the animal trait, and you can’t make Strikes. You can Dismiss the effect to return to your normal shape, and you resume your normal shape automatically if you’re reduced to 0 Hit Points.You gain the following statistics and abilities:
  • AC = 20 + your level. Ignore your armor’s check penalty and Speed reduction.
  • Fly speed 25 feet.
  • Weakness 5 to physical damage.
  • Low-light vision and imprecise scent 30 feet.
  • Acrobatics and Stealth modifiers of +10, unless your own is higher; Athletics modifier –4.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

[Ascended Celestial Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7331)

**Trigger**

---

You’re nigh invincible, and it’s clear that your foe is so far beneath you that they have no hope of winning. Spend 1 [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320). The triggering [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) becomes a regular hit instead of a critical hit and you gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) to physical damage equal to your level until the beginning of your next turn. During your next turn, if you attempt a [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395) check against the triggering creature, you do so at mythic proficiency.

<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Prerequisites**

**Requirements**
You are mounted and have a creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90).

</column>

---

Your mount attempts an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check to [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=2382) the creature you’ve grabbed or restrained, then Strides. The grabbed or restrained creature keeps that condition and is pulled to a space within your reach. This is forced movement. If the grabbed or restrained creature is [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88), it takes 2 slashing damage for every 5 feet it moved.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Absorb Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=1138) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 114

**Archetype** [Spellmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=32)

**Frequency**
once per 10 minutes

**Prerequisites**
[Spellmaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1134); spell repertoire or ability to prepare spells

**Trigger**
You critically succeed at a saving throw against a foe’s spell, and that spell is of a level you can normally cast.

</column>

---

You absorb a spell and store it in your body. If you are a spontaneous spellcaster, you can cast the triggering spell once during the next 10 minutes, even if it’s not on your spell list as if it were in your repertoire. If you are a prepared spellcaster, you can replace one of your prepared spells of the same level with the absorbed spell, but you must cast the absorbed spell within 10 minutes or you lose that spell slot for the day. You cast the spell at the same spell level as the spell you absorbed, but the spell is of your magical tradition and uses your spell DC, spell attack roll, and other statistics to determine its effects.

<title level="2">Absorb Spell leads to...</title>
[Retain Absorbed Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=2249)

    right="Feat 9"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Absorb Toxin](/Feats.aspx?ID=2826) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Grippli" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=264" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [The Mwangi Expanse](/Sources.aspx?ID=89) pg. 121

**Prerequisites**
You are not immune to [diseases](/Traits.aspx?ID=46) or [poisons](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)

**Trigger**
You attempt a saving throw against a disease or poison effect that affects an area.

</column>

---

Your skin readily absorbs poison and can consciously draw toxins into your body to spare others. Attempt a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) check against the triggering effect; your counteract level equals half your level (rounded up), and for the roll use either your class DC –10 or your spellcasting ability modifier plus your spellcasting proficiency bonus. If you counteract the triggering effect, you end the effect for all other creatures in the area; however, you must still save against the effect with a –2 penalty to the initial save.

Your time spent in the hostile parts of the world has inured you to extreme climates. In your favored terrain, you gain resistance equal to half your level to all [environmental damage](/Rules.aspx?ID=642) and are affected by temperature effects as though they were one step less severe (incredible heat or cold becomes extreme, extreme heat or cold becomes severe, and so on). When other creatures [Follow the Expert](/Actions.aspx?ID=514) with you as a guide in your favored terrain, they too treat temperature effects as one step less severe.

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

---

You've trained to serve as a mount, if only for your most trusted allies. When another PC rides you as a mount, your expert coordination allows them to gain three actions at the start of their turn, rather than the two they normally would for riding another PC (see [Riding PCs](/Rules.aspx?ID=3272)). You still gain only two actions at the start of your turn, instead of three, as you spend one action keeping them balanced on your back and ensuring they're firmly mounted.

You use your performances to supplement an ally's spellcasting, providing magical energy for their spells. Attempt a [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) check, using a [very high DC for the ally's level](/Rules.aspx?ID=552), and either spend a Focus Point (if the triggering spell is a focus spell) or expend a spell slot at least 1 level higher than the triggering spell. If you succeed at the Performance check, your ally's spell doesn't cost the Focus Point or spell slot.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 169

**Archetype** [Curse Maelstrom](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=190)

**Prerequisites**
[Curse Maelstrom Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3829)

</column>

---

When the curse within you spills out, you can lay curses on others and claim them for yourself with ease. You can cast [_claim curse_](/Spells.aspx?ID=884). At 10th level, you can also cast [_seal fate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=715), and at 12th level, you can also cast [_inevitable disaster_](/Spells.aspx?ID=930). You can cast these spells once per day as occult innate spells, but only while within your curse maelstrom state. If you couldn't already cast occult spells, these spells use Wisdom as your spellcasting ability, and you become trained in spell attack rolls and spell DCs for occult spells.

You've learned to harness the supernatural curse that animates you, imbuing your most powerful attacks with a terrible curse. When you critically hit with a fist Strike, negative energy binds to it; this is a [curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=38) and a [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46). Of the additional options below, only Prayer Attack is available freely to Red Mantis assassins without prior permission from the Blood Mistress. Those who dare learn these rare abilities without her permission run the risk of being cast out of the society and hunted down by their former allies. In theory, a daring infiltration of the Crimson Citadel could allow one to study hidden texts and learn these techniques, but the chambers within and below this fortress are among the most dangerous in the region, so such an attempt should not be made lightly!

**Source** [Firebrands](/Sources.aspx?ID=196) pg. 81 **Archetype** [Celebrity](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=245) **Prerequisites** [Celebrity Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1931); [Mesmerizing Gaze](/Feats.aspx?ID=1933) **Access** Members of the Firebrands at the rank of second mark or higher have access to this feat. --- Your reputation as a Firebrand precedes you, and you need only make a simple gesture or give a look of recognition to amaze those around you. You're so famous and beloved that even your enemies are fans, and they're shocked to see you here. Choose one target creature who can see you to acknowledge. The target must attempt a Will save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. Regardless of the result, the target becomes temporarily immune to Acknowledge Fan for 1 minute. **Special** This feat has either the [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11) or [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120) trait, matching the choice you made when you took Mesmerizing Gaze. **Critical Success** The target is unaffected and becomes temporarily immune to Acknowledge Fan for 1 day.
**Success** The target is [stunned 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36) and becomes temporarily immune to Acknowledge Fan for 1 day.
**Failure** The target is stunned 2.
**Critical Failure** The target is [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28) until the end of your next turn.

[Acquired Tolerance](/Feats.aspx?ID=2040) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Fortune" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=76" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 186

**Archetype** [Poisoner](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=71)

**Prerequisites**
[Poisoner Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2036)

**Trigger**
You fail a save against a poison.

</column>

---

A small amount of poison, taken at nonlethal doses, can help the body build up a resistance against a more deadly dosage. Reroll the triggering check and use the second result. Once you use Acquired Tolerance, you can continue to use it against the same type of poison that day, but you can't use it against a different type of poison until after you make your next daily preparations. For instance, if you used the reaction on a save against [giant scorpion venom](/Equipment.aspx?ID=114), you could use it again against giant scorpion venom even if it came from a different source, but you couldn't use it against [nettleweed residue](/Equipment.aspx?ID=124), [lich dust](/Equipment.aspx?ID=121), or another poison.

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 108 **Prerequisites** Trained in [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42) **Access** Tian Xia origin --- You’ve studied the routes by which qi flows through the body. The needles stored in your healer’s tools can manipulate its flow and improve health when applied to specific meridian points. You spend a day studying an ally to attempt a [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42) check to improve their qi against a standard DC for your ally’s level. The ally is then immune to all uses of Acupuncturist for 1 week. **Critical Success** You grant your ally the choice of a +2 circumstance bonus to one downtime activity skill check within the next week, or the ability to roll twice on their next saving throw within the next week against an affliction and take the higher result; this is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612) effect.
**Success** You grant your ally a +1 circumstance bonus to one downtime activity skill check within the next week.
**Critical Failure** Your ally takes a –1 circumstance penalty to all downtime activity skill checks within the next week.

You spend a day studying an ally to attempt a Medicine check to improve their qi against a standard DC for your ally’s level. The ally is then immune to all uses of Acupuncturist for 1 week. Critical Success You grant your ally the choice of a +2 circumstance bonus to one downtime activity skill check within the next week, or the ability to roll twice on their next saving throw within the next week against an affliction and take the higher result; this is a fortune effect. Success You grant your ally a +1 circumstance bonus to one downtime activity skill check within the next week. Critical Failure Your ally takes a –1 circumstance penalty to all downtime activity skill checks within the next week.

Through study of multiple magical traditions, you’ve altered a spell to suit your spellcasting style. Choose one cantrip from a magical tradition other than your own. If you prepare spells, you can choose this spell when you prepare your cantrips, in addition to your other options. If you have a spell repertoire, replace one of your cantrips known with the chosen spell. You can cast this cantrip as a spell of your class’s tradition.

If you swap or retrain this cantrip later, you can choose its replacement from the same alternate tradition or a different one.

If you prepare spells without a spellbook (if you're a [cleric](/Classes.aspx?ID=5) or [druid](/Classes.aspx?ID=6), for example), one of your cantrips must always be the chosen spell, and you prepare the rest normally. You can cast this cantrip as a spell of your class's tradition.

 If you swap or retrain this cantrip later, you can choose its replacement from the same alternate tradition or a different one.

[Adaptive Adept](/Feats.aspx?ID=4481) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Human" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=90" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 64

**Prerequisites**
[Adapted Cantrip](/Feats.aspx?ID=4474); can cast 3rd-level spells

</column>

---

You’ve continued adapting your magic to blend your class’s tradition with your adapted tradition. Choose a cantrip or 1st-rank spell from the same magical tradition as your cantrip from [Adapted Cantrip](/Feats.aspx?ID=66). You gain that spell, adding it to your spell options just like the cantrip from Adapted Cantrip. You can cast this spell as a spell of your class’s magical tradition. If you choose a 1st-rank spell, you don’t gain access to the heightened versions of that spell, meaning you can’t prepare them if you prepare spells and you can’t learn them or select the spell as a signature spell if you have a spell repertoire.

---

After years of using black powder weaponry in dimly lit spaces, you’ve become accustomed to dazzling flashes of light and sudden shifts in illumination. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against visual effects. If you roll a success on a saving throw against a [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727) effect, you get a critical success instead.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 3"
    pfs=""
>
[Additional Circus Trick](/Feats.aspx?ID=2688) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Circus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=375" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Come One, Come All, to the Extinction Curse Player's Guide!](/Sources.aspx?ID=83)

**Prerequisites**
You must have a signature trick

</column>

---

Your signature trick can have one additional trait beyond the number provided in Table 2: Trick Progression on page 63 of _Pathfinder #151: The Show Must Go On_. If the trick trait has an associated skill (such as [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) with the [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) trait) and that skill is one of your trick checks, your checks with that skill to Perform a Trick aren't penalized if you Perform a Trick using a different skill. For example, if your signature trick has [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) and Intimidation as trick checks and you take this feat to add the fire trait, you can Perform a Trick using Acrobatics (at no penalty), then Acrobatics again (at a -5 penalty), and then Intimidation (at no penalty).

</column>

---

Another follower joins you in your travels. They are a [novice follower](/Followers.aspx) that has the [minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=653) trait. 

**Special** You can select this feat more than once, gaining an additional follower each time, to a maximum of four total followers.

<title level="3">Multiple Followers</title> The captain archetype gives you the opportunity to have multiple followers at one time—up to four followers— but only one of those followers, your “active follower,” participates in combat or exploration activities; the rest hang back, ready to be called upon if needed. As soon as you gain a second follower from the captain archetype, you also gain Call Follower to switch your active follower.

You descend from the rare psychic vampires known as vetalaranas. **Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 202

**Prerequisites**
Master in [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9)

</column>

---

You use your medical training to ameliorate sickness or assuage fears. When you use [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9) to [Administer First Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=54), instead of Stabilizing a character or Stopping Bleeding, you can reduce an ally's [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) or [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34) condition by 2, or remove either of those conditions entirely on a critical success. You can remove only one condition at a time. The DC for the Medicine check is usually the DC of the effect that caused the condition.

You dig deeper into the magical tools found in wizard schools and divine domains. You gain an advanced focus spell, either the [necromancer](/ArcaneSchools.aspx?ID=7) advanced school spell [_life siphon_](/Spells.aspx?ID=532) or the advanced domain spell of the [death domain](/Domains.aspx?ID=7), [_eradicate undeath_](/Spells.aspx?ID=420). Increase the number of Focus Points in your focus pool by 1. If you choose _life siphon_, it triggers when you expend spell slots from your class even if they aren't wizard spell slots.

**Special** You can select this feat a second time, choosing the other advanced focus spell.

---

You gain access to a powerful new school spell depending on your arcane school. If you’re an abjurer, you gain [_energy absorption_](/Spells.aspx?ID=528); if you’re a conjurer, you gain [_dimensional steps_](/Spells.aspx?ID=524); if you’re a diviner, you gain [_vigilant eye_](/Spells.aspx?ID=536); if you’re an enchanter, you gain [_dread aura_](/Spells.aspx?ID=526); if you’re an evoker, you gain [_elemental tempest_](/Spells.aspx?ID=527); if you’re an illusionist, you gain [_invisibility cloak_](/Spells.aspx?ID=531); if you’re a necromancer, you gain [_life siphon_](/Spells.aspx?ID=532); and if you’re a transmuter, you gain [_shifting form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=535). Increase the number of Focus Points in your focus pool by 1.

When an enemy's movement is compromised, you deliver a more deadly blow. Make a Strike against a creature that is [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20), [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31), or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=33). You gain a circumstance bonus to damage on this Strike equal to the number of weapon damage dice, or that number + 2 if you're wielding the weapon in two hands. <traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=615" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=695" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #223: Hell's Destiny](/Sources.aspx?ID=336) pg. 230

**Prerequisites**
Master in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37); [Quick Repair](/Feats.aspx?ID=5198)

</column>

---

You tinker, create, and repair gear as you adventure. You can spend part of your daily preparations adjusting your group’s equipment. This allows you to attempt to [Repair](/Actions.aspx?ID=2384) up to five items during that time.

You gain access to a new exploration activity: Tinker on the Go. So long as you have two free hands and have access to the necessary tools, you can make Crafting progress while out traveling. At the GM’s discretion, you might not be able to Tinker on the Go for projects that require extensive infrastructure, such as a smithing forge. Otherwise, time spent exploring can count toward a day of crafting progress, as long as 8 hours of time get used in this way. 

If you lead a [troop](/Rules.aspx?ID=3439), you maintain their equipment in addition to your companions’ gear. Once per day when you Command the troop in a skirmish encounter, you can increase the DC of their offensive actions by 1 until the beginning of your next turn.

fields.text: Feat 7 Adventurous Outfitter May contain spoilers from Hell's Destiny Uncommon General Skill Source Pathfinder #223: Hell's Destiny pg. 230 Prerequisites Master in Crafting; Quick Repair You tinker, create, and repair gear as you adventure. You can spend part of your daily preparations adjusting your group’s equipment. This allows you to attempt to Repair up to five items during that time. You gain access to a new exploration activity: Tinker on the Go. So long as you have two free hands and have access to the necessary tools, you can make Crafting progress while out traveling. At the GM’s discretion, you might not be able to Tinker on the Go for projects that require extensive infrastructure, such as a smithing forge. Otherwise, time spent exploring can count toward a day of crafting progress, as long as 8 hours of time get used in this way. If you lead a troop, you maintain their equipment in addition to your companions’ gear. Once per day when you Command the troop in a skirmish encounter, you can increase the DC of their offensive actions by 1 until the beginning of your next turn.

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 115 **Archetype** [Ascended Celestial](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=289) **Prerequisites** [Ascended Celestial Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7331) **Requirements** Your nimbus is active. --- You transfer a portion of your divine spark to an ally, temporarily dimming your nimbus to encase an ally in a barrier of light that repels attackers. Select a willing creature within the [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2402) of your nimbus. You surround the target in a protective barrier of light; this is a 10-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) centered on the target. This barrier lasts for 1 minute, or until you [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) it. While the Aegis of the Innocent is active, the area of your nimbus is halved. The target gains a +1 status bonus to AC. Any enemy within the barrier, or entering the barrier, must attempt a Fortitude saving throw against your class DC or your spell DC. A creature needs to attempt this save only once each round. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature becomes [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) for 1 round and treats the space within the barrier as [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366).
**Failure** The creature becomes [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) for 1 minute, is pushed 10 feet, and treats the space within the barrier as difficult terrain. If a creature would be pushed into a solid barrier or another creature, it stops at that point and takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the creature is also [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) for 1 round.

>
[Aeonbound](/Feats.aspx?ID=7195) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Lineage" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=641" />
<trait label="Nephilim" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=518" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 52

</column>

---

Your lineage is influenced or directly tied to the supernatural inhabitants of the Perfect City of Axis, a realm of pure and absolute order. This energy suffuses your body and helps it maintain coherency, resisting effects that would undermine your function or mar your otherwise orderly form. You and your allies can [Treat your Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=2399) without a [healer's toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2727). Once per day, when someone rolls a failure or a critical failure on a check to Treat your Wounds, you can focus on your internal cohesion to increase the degree of success by one step.

<title level="2">Aeonbound leads to...</title>
[Channel the Godmind](/Feats.aspx?ID=7217), [Impose Order (Nephilim)](/Feats.aspx?ID=7216), [Intuitive Crafting](/Feats.aspx?ID=7200), [Methodical Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=7213), [Resilient Physiology](/Feats.aspx?ID=7207)

    right="Feat 1"

>
[Aerial Boomerang](/Feats.aspx?ID=4206) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Air" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=5" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 24

</column>

---

A blade of shearing wind races away from you in a 60-foot line. Each creature in the area takes 2d4 slashing damage with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your class DC. In the final square of the line, the boomerang whirls in place until the end of your next turn. Any creature that ends its turn in that square has to save against the boomerang.

 On your next turn, you can use a single action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait, to return the boomerang to you. It returns in a line from its square to your current location, with the same effect as the initial line, then the impulse ends. You must have line of effect to the boomerang and be within 60 feet of it.

---
**Level (+2)** The damage increases by 1d4.

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 202

**Prerequisites**
Master in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1)

</column>

---

You move with grace in flight and can perform amazing aerial stunts. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) checks to [Maneuver in Flight](/Actions.aspx?ID=30) and can combine two maneuvers into a single action, such as reversing direction while making a steep ascent or descent or hovering in gale-force winds. The DC of the Acrobatics check is equal to the DC of the most difficult maneuver + 5. If you're legendary in Acrobatics, you can combine three such maneuvers into a single action; the DC of the Acrobatics check is equal to the DC of the most difficult maneuver + 10. Regardless of the combination, these maneuvers rarely allow you to move farther than your fly Speed.

You can open your internal nexus, unleashing a destructive beam of magical energy that emanates from your hand, eyes, or chest. You fire a beam that deals 6d6 force damage in a 60- foot [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388) and pushes back anyone who stands within. Each creature in the area must attempt a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save against your nexus DC. A creature that fails is also pushed back 10 feet (20 feet on a critical failure). The damage increases by 2d6 at 10th level and every 2 levels thereafter. You are no longer overflowing.

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 105

**Archetype** [Veil Dancer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=395)

**Prerequisites**
[Veil Dancer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9363)

**Trigger**
You use an action or cast a spell with the [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710) trait.

</column>

---

You leave behind an afterimage of yourself in your previous square. This afterimage looks like you and can perform simple behaviors to make the deception more plausible but otherwise cannot move or take actions. A creature can distinguish between you and your afterimage easily. Your afterimage automatically fails all checks and DCs and is destroyed if it would take any damage; otherwise, it lasts for 1 minute. Whenever you take the [Step](/Actions.aspx?ID=2304) action, you can instead teleport to an afterimage instead. If you do, the action gains the [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710) trait, and the afterimage you teleport to is destroyed.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Elf" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=58" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 40

</column>

---

You work at a pace born from longevity that enhances your thoroughness. You can voluntarily spend twice as much time as normal on a Perception check or skill check to gain a +2 circumstance bonus to that check. You also don't treat a natural 1 as worse than usual on these checks; you get a critical failure only if your result is 10 lower than the DC. For example, you could get these benefits if you spent 2 actions to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84), which normally takes 1 action. You can get these benefits during exploration by taking twice as long exploring as normal, or in downtime by spending twice as much downtime.

 The GM might determine a situation doesn't grant you a benefit if a delay would be directly counterproductive to your success, such as a tense negotiation with an impatient creature.

<trait label="Elf" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=58" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 48

</column>

---

You work at a pace born from longevity that enhances your thoroughness. You can voluntarily spend twice as much time as normal on a Perception check or skill check that takes 1 action or longer. If you do, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to the check and don't automatically reduce your degree of success on a natural 1 (you get a critical failure only if your result is 10 lower than the DC). For example, you could get these benefits if you spent 2 actions to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84), which normally takes 1 action. You can get these benefits during exploration by taking twice as long exploring as normal, or in downtime by spending twice as much downtime.

The GM might determine a situation doesn't grant you a benefit if a delay would be directly counterproductive to your success, such as a tense negotiation with an impatient creature.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fighter" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=71" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 145

**Trigger**
You use the [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=839) reaction, and the opponent that triggered Shield Block is adjacent to you and is your size or smaller.

</column>

---

You push back as you block the attack, knocking your foe away or off balance. You use your shield to push the triggering creature, either automatically [Shoving](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) it 5 feet or causing it to become [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) until the start of your next turn. The triggering creature chooses whether to be moved or become flat-footed. If it chooses to be moved, you choose the direction. If the Shove would cause it to hit a solid object, enter a square of difficult terrain, or enter another creature's space, it must become flat-footed instead of being moved.

<title level="2">Aggressive Block leads to...</title>
[Flinging Shove](/Feats.aspx?ID=408), [Powerful Shove](/Feats.aspx?ID=373)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Archetype** [Spell Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=126)

**Prerequisites**
[Spell Trickster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3368); ability to cast [_mage hand_](/Spells.aspx?ID=177)

</column>

---

When you cast _mage hand_, you can modify its target to be a set of [thieves' tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=58). When you Cast the Spell in this way, the tools move up to 20 feet towards a device or lock. After you Sustain the Spell on future turns, you can use the tools to attempt [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) checks to [Disable a Device](/Actions.aspx?ID=69) or [Pick a Lock](/Actions.aspx?ID=70) within the spell's range, but you take a –2 penalty to your Thievery check. If you critically fail, the spell ends and you can't use this modification again for 24 hours.

<title level="2">Agile Hand leads to...</title>
[Larcenous Hand](/Feats.aspx?ID=3384)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Champion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=24" />
<trait label="Fighter" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=71" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Knights of Lastwall](/Sources.aspx?ID=123) pg. 82

**Archetypes** [Bastion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=240) (Level 4), [Bastion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=49) (Level 4)

**Access**
Knights of Lastwall have access to this feat.

**Requirements**
You are wielding a shield with a [shield boss](/Weapons.aspx?ID=41) or [shield spikes](/Weapons.aspx?ID=42) in one hand.

</column>

---

You change your grip on the shield, allowing you to combine rapid attacks with your shield boss or shield spikes and your main weapon's Strikes in a series of swift motions. You reduce your shield boss and shield spikes weapon damage die to 1d4. As long as the weapon damage die is 1d4, your shield boss and shield spike Strikes gain the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170) weapon trait. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Air" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=5" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 24

**Trigger**
A creature within 60 feet is falling.

</column>

---

Air currents flow upward to slow the target's fall to 60 feet per round. The cushion ends when the target reaches the ground, and the creature takes no damage from the fall. The cushion expires if the creature doesn't reach the ground within 1 minute, but any distance it fell during that minute doesn't count for any damage the creature would take from the fall. You can't use Air Cushion again while you have one in effect.

---
**Level (8th)** The range is 120 feet, and you can create cushions for up to 5 falling creatures with one reaction.

Turbulent air suffuses your kinetic aura. This doesn't displace other matter but provides air for creatures in your kinetic aura that need air to breathe. Air in your kinetic aura is [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) for flying creatures other than yourself.

**Trigger**

</column>

---

You create a blanket of fog in a 5–foot burst centered on one corner of your space. All creatures within that area are [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4), and all others are concealed to them. [Alchemical Discoveries](/Feats.aspx?ID=1456) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 61

**Prerequisites**
[alchemical sciences methodology](/Methodologies.aspx?ID=1)

</column>

---

You've devoted extra time in the lab to improve your knowledge of alchemy. You learn the formulas for two alchemical items each time you level up instead of one; these must still be [elixirs](/Equipment.aspx?Category=6&Subcategory=8) or [tools](/Equipment.aspx?Category=6&Subcategory=10). The number of versatile vials you can create each day increases by 1 if you're an expert in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4), 2 if you're a master, or 3 if you're legendary.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Alchemical Familiar](/Feats.aspx?ID=5760) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=812" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 63

</column>

---

You have used alchemy to create life, a simple creature formed from alchemical materials, reagents, and a bit of your own blood. You gain a [familiar](/Rules.aspx?ID=2121), which has the [construct](/Familiars.aspx?ID=109) familiar ability; this is permanent, doesn't require the familiar to have the [tough](/Familiars.aspx?ID=148) familiar ability, and doesn't count against your usual limit of familiar abilities (typically 2). The familiar uses your Intelligence modifier to determine its Perception, [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34), and [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) modifiers.

---

You have used alchemy to create life, a simple creature formed from alchemical materials, reagents, and a bit of your own blood. This alchemical familiar appears to be a small creature of flesh and blood, though it might have some unusual or distinguishing aspects depending on your creative process. Like other familiars, your alchemical familiar assists you in your laboratory and on adventures. The familiar uses your Intelligence modifier to determine its Perception, Acrobatics, and Stealth modifiers (see [Familiars](/Familiars.aspx) for more information).

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Alchemical Revivification](/Feats.aspx?ID=5803) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=812" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 69

</column>

---

If you die while under the effect of at least one [elixir](/Traits.aspx?ID=589), the alchemical compounds in your bloodstream bring you back to life at the start of your next turn. You're affected by an [elixir of rejuvenation](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3309), then a [true elixir of life](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3308), then your choice of a [major bestial mutagen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3315), [major juggernaut mutagen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3318), or [major quicksilver mutagen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3319) as though you just imbibed it. These automatic reactions don't get any special benefits you add when creating or using these items. Because you died, all other alchemical compounds in your bloodstream are inert. After being revived, you're temporarily immune to Alchemical Rejuvenation for 1d4 hours.

<traits>

---

You can identify alchemical items quickly. When using the Crafting skill to Identify Alchemy on an alchemical item you hold, you can do so as a single action, which has the concentrate and manipulate traits, instead of spending 10 minutes. If you have the formula for the item you are attempting to identify, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your check, and if you roll a critical failure, you get a failure instead.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Alchemical Shot](/Feats.aspx?ID=3165) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Gunslinger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=406" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 112

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) For the gunslinger’s Alchemical Shot feat and any similar abilities that change a weapon’s damage type, only the primary damage’s type is affected; any secondary effects (such as precision damage or damage applied from a rune) are not affected._

**Requirements**
You have an alchemical [bomb](/Equipment.aspx?Category=6&amp;Subcategory=7) worn or in one hand, and are wielding a firearm or crossbow.

</column>

---

You've practiced a technique for mixing alchemical bombs with your loaded shot. You Interact to retrieve the bomb (if it's not already in your hand) and pour its contents onto your ammunition, consuming the bomb, then resume your grip on the required weapon. Next, Strike with your firearm. The Strike deals damage of the same type as the bomb (for instance, fire damage for [alchemist's fire](/Equipment.aspx?ID=75)), and it deals an additional 1d6 [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) of the same type as the bomb. If the Strike is a failure, you take 1d6 damage of the same type as the bomb you used, and the firearm [misfires](/Rules.aspx?ID=1649).

 The persistent damage increases to 2d6 if the bomb is 11th level or higher, or 3d6 if it's 17th level or higher.

---

You are an Aldori swordlord. You can always obtain free room and board at the Aldori Academy for yourself and your allies.  You can use Dueling [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) instead of Diplomacy to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) or [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=2393) provided that the target you are Making an Impression on would be aware of the Aldori swordlords or your Request is related to your standing as a swordlord. **Special** You can’t take both this feat and [Swordlord Exile](/Feats.aspx?ID=7912).

fields.text: Feat 1 Alghollthu Bound Azarketi Source Absalom, City of Lost Omens pg. 394, Azarketi Ancestry Web Supplement pg. 4 Although you may not even be aware, the alghollthus your ancestors once served maintain a stranglehold on the deepest, tethered parts of your mind. You receive a +2 circumstance bonus to Will saves against mental effects that would make you controlled, and if you roll a success against such an effect, you get a critical success instead. >
[Align Armament](/Feats.aspx?ID=286) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Cleric" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=26" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 124

**Frequency**
once per round

**Prerequisites**
chaotic, evil, good, or lawful deity

</column>

---

You bring a weapon into metaphysical concordance with your deity’s beliefs. When you select this feat, choose chaotic, evil, good, or lawful. Your choice must match one of your deity’s alignment components. This action has the trait corresponding to the chosen alignment component.

 When you use this action, you touch a weapon. For 1 round, that weapon deals an additional 1d6 damage of the chosen type to creatures of the opposed alignment. For example, if you chose good, the weapon would deal an extra 1d6 good damage to evil creatures. If you Align an Armament again, any previously aligned armament loses its additional damage.

**Special** You can select this feat a second time, choosing your deity’s other alignment component. When you Align an Armament, you can choose either alignment component.

<title level="2">Align Armament leads to...</title>
[Extend Armament Alignment](/Feats.aspx?ID=299)

>
[Alkenstar Agent Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3568) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Outlaws of Alkenstar</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #178: Punks in a Powderkeg](/Sources.aspx?ID=119) pg. 78

**Archetype** [Alkenstar Agent](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=183)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5); trained at least one [firearm](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=16)

**Access**
You have been initiated by the grand duchess of Alkenstar or one of her agents.

</column>

---

You put on the persona of a rough and tumble outlaw, but your real goals are to report threats to Alkenstar back to the grand duchess. You become an expert in Deception and trained in your choice of Underworld [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) or Legal Lore; if you were already trained, you become an expert instead. You gain the [Lie to Me](/Feats.aspx?ID=811) skill feat.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you've gained two other feats from the Alkenstar Agent archetype.

<title level="2">Alkenstar Agent Dedication leads to...</title>
[Flash your Badge](/Feats.aspx?ID=3571), [Loose Cannon](/Feats.aspx?ID=3569), [Prepare Papers](/Feats.aspx?ID=3570)

    right="Feat 18"

>
[All in my Head](/Feats.aspx?ID=1660) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Bard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=19" />
<trait label="Illusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=92" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=106" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 115

**Trigger**
You would take damage from a Strike or spell that doesn't have the [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40) trait or otherwise cause instant death (such as [_disintegrate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=76)).

</column>

---

Using your occult connections and incredible powers of persuasion, you convince yourself that the triggering damage is a figment of your imagination. The damage changes from its usual damage type to mental damage, and the damaging effect gains the [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188) trait. You can't use this reaction if you are immune to [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) effects or mental damage.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[All of the Animal](/Feats.aspx?ID=3422) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Quest for the Frozen Flame</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #175: Broken Tusk Moon](/Sources.aspx?ID=112) pg. 78

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16)

</column>

---

You know how to make the best and most efficient use of a hunted animal's carcass. Choose a Large or larger corpse of an [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=9) that died within the past day. While using Survival to [Subsist](/Actions.aspx?ID=27) near the carcass, you always receive enough food for yourself and one additional Medium creature, using up the meat from the carcass to do so. Since you're using all of the animal, others can't use the carcass's meat for any other purpose, including their own use of All of the Animal.

<title level="2">Skill Feats</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #175: Broken Tusk Moon](/Sources.aspx?ID=112) pg. 78

Characters can gain access to the following new skill feats throughout “Broken Tusk Moon.”

 **All of the Animal**: Head scout Wipa teaches this skill feat to characters who help her butcher an animal for meat, such as the moose at the beginning of the adventure or another animal slain throughout the course of the Broken Tusk following's journey.

 **Spirit Speaker**: Mammoth Lord Argakoa, also known as Argakoa the Songsinger, might teach a fraction of her tremendous skill to a young scout who joins her in song. 

**Tame Animal**: The young herd tender Imek has a natural way with animals. She is happy to teach what she knows to any characters who display a similar reverence toward living creatures, such as by peacefully resolving their encounter with the giant porcupine in Chapter 1 of this adventure. Although this feat is particularly useful to characters who want to recruit animal followers throughout the Quest for the Frozen Flame Adventure Path, it isn't strictly necessary for the party to succeed in their adventures. It can be a great boon to parties taking part in other quests, as well.

**Related Feats**: [Spirit Speaker](/Feats.aspx?ID=3423), [Tame Animal](/Feats.aspx?ID=3424)

<traits>
<trait label="Death" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=40" />
<trait label="Fire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=72" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 29

White-hot fire consumes everything in a cataclysmic sphere of death. The fire fills your choice of a 30-foot burst within 500 feet or a 30-foot emanation. This deals 13d6 fire damage with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your class DC. Any creature dropped to 0 HP by this fire dies, reduced to a pile of ash.

 If you die to this impulse, you return to life at the start of your next turn in the same space. When you return, you have Hit Points equal to double your level.

---
**Level (20th)** The damage is 15d6.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[All the Time in the World](/Feats.aspx?ID=2744) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Fists of the Ruby Phoenix</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Investigator" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=318" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #168: King of the Mountain](/Sources.aspx?ID=87) pg. 75

**Frequency**
once per hour

</column>

---

Your firsthand experience of the subjective nature of time and space has given you new observational insights. Your mind processes information so quickly that time appears to stop for all creatures but you. You can take up to 9 actions in 3 sets of up to 3 actions each. During this time, you can use purely mental and observational abilities such as [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26), [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84), and [Devise a Stratagem](/Actions.aspx?ID=546), and you can use an action to move a mental projection of yourself to a location within a 60- foot radius to observe objects more closely and from different angles, though you can't affect your surroundings in any way (for instance, you could move your mental projection more closely to a distant door to read a minute inscription on its handle, but you could not open it to observe the other side). When the duration elapses, time resumes its normal flow.

<title level="2">Capstone Feats</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #168: King of the Mountain](/Sources.aspx?ID=87) pg. 75

Player characters can select one of the following new class feats for their 20th-level class feat upon entering the _Glass Lighthouse_ or by meditating on the cushion in area H4.

**Related Feats**: [Dance of Intercession](/Feats.aspx?ID=2745), [Demon's Hair](/Feats.aspx?ID=2746), [Everdistant Defense](/Feats.aspx?ID=2747), [Extradimensional Stash](/Feats.aspx?ID=2748), [Head of the Night Parade](/Feats.aspx?ID=2749), [Heart of the Kaiju](/Feats.aspx?ID=2750), [Plum Deluge](/Feats.aspx?ID=2751), [Ruby Resurrection](/Feats.aspx?ID=2752), [Scapegoat Parallel Self](/Feats.aspx?ID=2753), [Sever Space](/Feats.aspx?ID=2754), [Time Dilation Cascade](/Feats.aspx?ID=2755), [Vitality-Manipulating Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=2756), [Vivacious Afterimage](/Feats.aspx?ID=2757), [Whirlwind Toss](/Feats.aspx?ID=2758), [Worldsphere Gravity](/Feats.aspx?ID=2759)

[Alloy Flesh and Steel](/Feats.aspx?ID=4263) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Metal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=505" />
<trait label="Polymorph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=127" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 31

</column>

---

Elemental energy replaces every cell of your body with raw metal. You gain the benefits of the [_ferrous form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1369) spell (except you can't cast [_needle darts_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1375)) until the end of your next turn. You can Sustain the impulse up to 1 minute, and when you do, you can [Raise](/Actions.aspx?ID=98) a metal Shield if you're wielding one. Your metal [Elemental Blasts](/Actions.aspx?ID=2125) deal an additional die of damage. If you suspend any conditions with Alloy Flesh and Steel, when it ends, you're temporarily immune to Alloy Flesh and Steel for 1 hour.

---
**Level (16th)** The resistance is 15.

>
[Alter Admixture](/Feats.aspx?ID=5782) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=812" />
<trait label="Exploration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=595" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 66

**Requirements**
You are holding or wearing an [alchemist's toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2702).

</column>

---

Sometimes, you need to adapt your alchemical mixtures to new situations. In a process that takes 10 minutes, you change an item you created with advanced alchemy into a similar item. You can change an [alchemical bomb](/Equipment.aspx?Category=6&Subcategory=7) into  another type of alchemical bomb, an [elixir](/Equipment.aspx?Category=6&Subcategory=8) into another type of elixir, or a [poison](/Equipment.aspx?Category=6&Subcategory=9) into another type of poison. If it's unclear whether two alchemical consumables are similar, the GM decides. You must know the formula for the new item, and the new item must be of the same or lower item level than the original item. The new item still keeps the [infused](/Traits.aspx?ID=797) trait, and it remains potent as long as the original item would have.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Alter Ego Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3807) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 126

**Archetype** [Alter Ego](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=187)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5); Trained in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15)

</column>

---

You make yourself into a living mirror, becoming a double of someone unremarkable, and you slip into exactly the role that can get you past security or into a sensitive facility. You become an expert in Deception. You gain the Assume a Role activity.

 **Assume a Role** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Requirements** You've spent at least 1 hour studying a creature whose role you intend to copy and have done so within the last 3 days. This could include meeting and learning from someone in that role, tailing and spying on someone, using magic to observe them at work, or some other method, as long as you have a visual source of information; **Effect** You quickly and accurately learn how to do mundane jobs or at least copy the movements enough to appear as if you do. A chosen role can take many forms—from cook, cleaner, or librarian to cult member, priest, or duke—but it's always a role and never a specific individual.

 You perform the [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) activity to pass as a member of the role you observed and gain a +1 circumstance bonus to any Deception checks you attempt in your impersonation. This takes the normal amount of time it takes you to Impersonate. You also choose one [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) skill relevant to that role (such as Farming Lore for a farmer). While in your role, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to checks for that Lore skill, and if you're untrained in it, you can use your level as your proficiency bonus. You stop assuming the role after 24 hours, if you start studying for a new role, or if you choose to.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you've gained two other feats from the alter ego archetype.

<title level="2">Alter Ego Dedication leads to...</title>
[Borrow Memories](/Feats.aspx?ID=3814), [Change of Face](/Feats.aspx?ID=3808), [Fake It Till You Make it](/Feats.aspx?ID=3809), [Illusory Identity](/Feats.aspx?ID=4149), [In Plain Sight](/Feats.aspx?ID=3810), [It Was Me All Along!](/Feats.aspx?ID=4152), [Muscle Mimicry](/Feats.aspx?ID=3812), [Sound Mirror](/Feats.aspx?ID=3811), [Swap Reflections](/Feats.aspx?ID=3813), [We're on the List](/Feats.aspx?ID=4132)

Extensive training against [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) has taught you to cover your weak points, even when you think that you're alone. You aren't [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) to [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22), [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39), or flanking undead of your level or lower. If all of your opponents are undead, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to initiative rolls; the GM determines whether to apply this bonus if undead are disguised as another type of creature, if another type of creature is disguised as undead, or if there are additional opponents you haven't noticed who aren't undead.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Ambush Bladderwort](/Feats.aspx?ID=4296) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Composite" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=501" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Plant" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=125" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Water" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=165" />
<trait label="Wood" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=508" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 36

</column>

---

You plant the seed of a giant bladderwort in an unoccupied square of ground or water within 30 feet. It lasts for 10 minutes. Using this impulse again ends any previous one. If a creature enters its square, the seed erupts into a voluminous, translucent plant that seals tight around the triggering creature and fills with water. Unless the creature succeeds at a Reflex save against your class DC, it's [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) within the bladderwort and must hold its breath or begin [drowning](/Rules.aspx?ID=468). The [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) DC is also your class DC. The plant has AC 10 and 50 Hit Points.

 If a creature dies inside it, the plant shrinks down, converting itself and the remains into a watery fruit. A creature can eat this consumable to regain 1d8+4 HP, after which that creature is temporarily immune for 10 minutes. This fruit rots after 1 hour.

---
**Level (+4)** The bladderwort's HP increase by 25 and the fruit's healing increases by 1d8+4.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Ambush Tactics](/Feats.aspx?ID=3905) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Kingmaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Kingmaker Companion Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=151) pg. 35

**Prerequisites**
trained in [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) about a specific terrain

</column>

---

You've made a study of the best practices for laying ambushes in terrains you've spent time learning about, be it the best way to ambush foes or the best methods of reacting to surprise attacks in those terrains. In any combat during which an enemy rolls [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) to determine initiative, you can choose to roll initiative using a Lore check that's appropriate for the encounter's terrain, if you're trained in the appropriate Lore skill.

<title level="2">Adventuring with Jubilost</title>

**Source** [Kingmaker Companion Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=151) pg. 35

Jubilost provides support in battle with his alchemical bombs and elixirs, but he's just as helpful when he spends time at home. As long as he's a companion, he'll serve as a source for alchemical items of his level or lower for purchase at regular prices, but if made Helpful, he provides these resources to the PCs at cost. His studies also result in the development of two new skill feats; while Jubilost doesn't take these feats himself (ever the theoretician), once the PCs have at least 4 Influence with him, these feats and formulas become available as PC options at the appropriate level.

**Related Feats**: [Efficient Explorer](/Feats.aspx?ID=3906)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs=""
>
[Ambushing Knockdown](/Feats.aspx?ID=2207) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Agents of Edgewatch</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=139" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #159: All or Nothing](/Sources.aspx?ID=48) pg. 75

**Prerequisites**
[ruffian racket](/Rackets.aspx?ID=1)

**Access**
Side with the Washboard Dogs in the gang conflict.

**Requirements**
You're wielding a melee weapon that deals bludgeoning damage and you're [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) from or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) by an enemy.

</column>

---

You emerge from hiding and deliver a blow that can knock an enemy sprawling to the ground. You Stride up to half your Speed, but you must end your movement next to a foe you're hidden from or undetected by. You then Strike that enemy with the required weapon; if you hit, the target is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31).

<title level="2">Gang Feats</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #159: All or Nothing](/Sources.aspx?ID=48) pg. 75

Street gangs in Absalom recruit amateur pickpockets, ruffians, and vandals who show promise in their specialties and operate well in tight groups.

 Rogue agents can gain access to some of the following rogue feats by successfully helping Maurrisa Jonne or Bloody Berleth eliminate their rival (see Chapter 1). Some of these feats, however, can be gained only by helping a particular side in the gang conflict.

**Related Feats**: [Coordinated Distraction](/Feats.aspx?ID=2210), [Deny Support](/Feats.aspx?ID=2209), [Slice and Swipe](/Feats.aspx?ID=2206), [Subtle Shank](/Feats.aspx?ID=2208)

fields.text: Feat 2 Amphibious Form Evolution Summoner Source Impossible Magic pg. 79 Your eidolon adapts to life on land and underwater. They gain the amphibious trait, allowing them to breathe in water and air and to avoid the normal –2 penalty for making bludgeoning and slashing unarmed Strikes underwater. They gain a swim Speed equal to their land Speed or 25 feet, whichever is less; if they’re normally aquatic, they gain a land Speed equal to their swim Speed or 25 feet, whichever is less.

Your healing energies empower attacks. An ally that recovers Hit Points from your [_lay on hands_](/Spells.aspx?ID=395) gains a +1 status bonus to their attack rolls and deals 1 additional spirit damage on all their Strikes until the end of their next turn. In addition, all their Strikes are holy until the end of their next turn.

You break down a specific individual's idiolect, memorizing their speech mannerisms and habits. Due to the intense character study required, you can't remember more than one idiolect at a time.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=139" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 135

**Prerequisites**
[sneak attack 2d6](/Classes.aspx?ID=10)

**Requirements**
You must have identified a creature with [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26).

</column>

---

Your knowledge of a creature's physiology and understanding of tactics helps you attack with pinpoint accuracy. You carefully study a creature that you've identified to scope out particularly weak points in its positioning or physical form. The next time you deal sneak attack damage to the chosen creature with a Strike before the end of your turn, add an additional 2d6 precision damage. At 11th and 17th levels, if your additional damage from sneak attack increases, increase the additional damage from Analyze Weakness to 3d6 at 11th level and 4d6 at 17th level.

---

By unraveling memories and connections passed down from your progenitors and buried within your unconscious mind, you learn to convert your inherent magic into psychic power. You can cast any innate spells you know from an ancestry feat or heritage using your psychic spellcasting components. When you do so, the spell's tradition becomes occult, if it wasn't already, and you can use your psychic spellcasting ability modifier instead of Charisma to determine your spell attack roll and spell DC.

Long-lived elves have seen civilizations rise and fall, often at the hands of outside forces. As a result, they have developed a wariness of others who might seek to influence or control them. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=701" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 96

**Archetype** [Undersea Privateer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=379)

**Prerequisites**
[Undersea Privateer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8915)

**Requirements**
You’re in or under water.

</column>

---

You tense your muscles to make yourself neutrally buoyant and more difficult to move. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your Fortitude or Reflex DC against attempts to [Reposition](/Actions.aspx?ID=2379) or [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380) you. This bonus also applies to saving throws against spells or effects that attempt to force you to move. If any effect would force you to move 10 feet or more, attempt a DC 11 flat check. On a success, you move only 5 feet. Additionally, you don't have to take a [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381) action each turn to avoid sinking or moving with the current.

    right="Feat 5"
    pfs="Standard"

[Anchoring Roots](/Feats.aspx?ID=2394) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Leshy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=225" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 42

</column>

---

Small roots sprout from your feet, steadying you as you move. You gain the [Steady Balance](/Feats.aspx?ID=845) skill feat, even if you aren't trained in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1), and you can use the Anchor action.

 **Anchor** <actions string="Single Action" /> **Effect** You send your roots deeper into the ground, making it harder for you to stumble. Until you move, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your Fortitude or Reflex DC against attempts to [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) or [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40) you (or a +4 circumstance bonus if you're a [root leshy](/Heritages.aspx?ID=102)). This bonus also applies to saving throws against spells or effects that attempt to move you or knock you [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). If an effect forces you to move, you move only half the normal distance, as some of the effort goes to tearing out the roots. At the GM's discretion, this ability might not work on ground that's more resilient than stone, such as metal flooring or magically-reinforced masonry.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 186

**Archetype** [Assassin](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=239)

**Prerequisites**
[Assassin Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6257)

</column>

---

All your Strikes against a creature you have Marked for Death have the [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) trait, causing the mark to be instantly killed when reduced to 0 Hit Points. In addition, if the creature is killed this way, attempts to communicate with it, return it to life, turn it into an undead, or otherwise disturb its afterlife fail unless the effect's [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) rank is higher than half your level rounded up, or originates from an artifact or a deity. Use the level you were when you killed the creature, even if your level is higher at the time the attempt was made.

>
[Angel of Vindication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3612) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Knights of Lastwall](/Sources.aspx?ID=123) pg. 80

**Archetype** [Assassin](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=48)

**Prerequisites**
[Assassin Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1890)

**Access**
Knights of Lastwall have access to this feat.

**Requirements**
Your mark is an [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) creature.

</column>

---

To aid with your mission of destroying undead, you've specialized in techniques to destroy them, much as other assassins learn to kill the living. When you Strike a [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) undead foe with a weapon that has the [backstabber](/Traits.aspx?ID=172) weapon trait, you deal 3 extra precision damage instead of 1. If the weapon is a +3 weapon, you deal 6 extra precision damage instead of 2. If you have the [Angel of Death](/Feats.aspx?ID=1893) feat, your attacks also instantly destroy undead at 0 Hit Points, and attempts for the undead to rejuvenate—such as via a [lich's](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=68) _soul cage_ or a [ghost's](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=51) rejuvenation ability—fail unless the effect's [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) level is higher than half your level when you killed the creature (rounded up), or originates from an [artifact](/Traits.aspx?ID=253) or deity. Finally, if you have the [Assassinate](/Feats.aspx?ID=1894) feat and an undead mark critically fails its save against your Assassinate, it is destroyed.

</title>

</traits>

**Archetype** [Kitharodian Actor](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=301)

**Prerequisites**
[Kitharodian Actor Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7456)

</column>

---

You participated in a performance of _The Leaping Lion_, a play focusing on Cyricas, the animal-loving adventurer who traveled with his ape friend Mardu and remains a favorite hero among Taldan youth. You become trained in Nature and a Lore skill related to a particular type of animal commonly used in show business (such as Canine Lore, Ursine Lore, or Primate Lore); if you were already trained in either, you become an expert in that skill instead. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to all checks to [Command an Animal](/Actions.aspx?ID=2400) and [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about creatures with the animal trait. You can use your chosen animal Lore to Command an Animal of that type.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 17"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Animal Shape](/Feats.aspx?ID=2498) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Beastkin" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=337" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 81

</column>

---

You have full control over your shape and can transform into your inherent animal. You can use Change Shape to enter an animal shape. When you gain this feat, choose either [_aerial form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=4), [_animal form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=10), [_dinosaur form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=72), or [_insect form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=163); after you choose a form, you can't change the form. While in animal shape, you gain the effects of a 5th-level casting of your chosen form spell, except you always transform into an animal matching your inherent animal and can use your humanoid form's AC if it's higher than what the animal form grants. If your inherent animal isn't among the animals listed in the form, you default to the statistics and abilities of the bird battle form, cat battle form, deinonychus battle form, or ant battle form for _aerial form_, _animal form_, _dinosaur form_, and _insect form_, respectively (at the GM's discretion, you instead default to a different form that is closest to your inherent animal). You can remain in animal shape indefinitely and can use Change Shape to return to your humanoid or hybrid shape at any time.

 If you have the [Critter Shape](/Feats.aspx?ID=2490) feat, you can choose to gain the effects of a 4th-level [_pest form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=217), can remain in critter shape indefinitely, and can return to your critter shape at any time after leaving the shape, just as you can with Animal Shape.

Your proficiency in unarmored defense increases to expert. When you are raging and unarmored, your skin transforms into a thick hide. You gain a +2 item bonus to AC (+3 if you have the greater juggernaut class feature). The thickness of your hide gives you a Dexterity modifier cap to your AC of +3. This item bonus to AC is cumulative with [_armor potency runes_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=278) on your [explorer's clothing](/Armor.aspx?ID=2), [_mage armor_](/Spells.aspx?ID=176), and [_bracers of armor_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=416).

</traits>

---

You move like an animal. Your Speed increases by 5 feet. In addition, you gain one of the following Speeds available to your inherent animal: climb, fly, or swim. You gain this Speed only while in your hybrid shape. The new movement is as fast as your standard Speed; for example, if you have a 30-foot Speed, you can gain a 30-foot climb Speed. If your inherent animal doesn't typically have a specific type of Speed, you can't gain it with this feat. If your inherent animal doesn't typically have a climb, fly, or swim Speed, your Speed increases by 10 feet instead.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Archetype** [Spell Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=126)

**Prerequisites**
[Spell Trickster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3368); ability to cast [_animate rope_](/Spells.aspx?ID=667)

</column>

---

When you cast _animate rope_, you can modify its target to be 1 [net](/Equipment.aspx?ID=681). If you do, replace the spell's standard effects with the following: You cause a net to animate and throw itself at a Medium or smaller creature within 20 feet of the net. Attempt a spell attack roll against the target's Reflex DC. On a success, the target is [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) and takes a –10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds until it [Escapes](/Actions.aspx?ID=79); on a critical success, it's also [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) until it Escapes. The Escape DC is equal to your spell DC as long as the spell lasts. Once the spell ends, the Escape DC returns to the normal DC for a net (usually 16), and a creature adjacent to the target can Interact to remove the net.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 56

**Archetype** [Animist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=280)

**Prerequisites**
Wisdom +2

</column>

---

You have formed a bond with an apparition and can cast [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579) spells. Choose a single [apparition](/Apparitions.aspx) from those available to the animist. You become bound to that apparition and can attune to it each day during your [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575) to become trained in its apparition skills. If you are 8th level, you are expert in its apparition skills while attuned to it, and if you are 16th level, you are a master in its apparition skills while attuned to it. You can spend 1 day of downtime ending your relationship with this apparition and bonding to a new one. 

You gain the [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) activity. You can prepare two common cantrips each day from the [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) spell list or any other divine cantrips you have access to, including the cantrip listed in your apparition's apparition spells. You're trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for animist archetype spells is Wisdom, and they are divine animist spells.

<title level="2">Animist Dedication leads to...</title>
[Basic Animist Spellcasting](/Feats.aspx?ID=7220), [Spiritual Awakening](/Feats.aspx?ID=7221)

While you are prone, you are always Taking Cover against ranged attacks, you ignore the status penalty on your attack rolls from being prone, and you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Athletics checks to Trip. You can choose to move up to half your Speed when you Crawl. You can instead move up to your full Speed when you Crawl, but if you do, you must succeed at a DC 6 flat check or your body deteriorates.

    right="Feat 18"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Annihilating Compound Invocation](/Feats.aspx?ID=9214) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Force" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=75" />
<trait label="Invocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=956" />
<trait label="Runesmith" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=952" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 53

</column>

---

Each tradition of magic holds sway over two of the four essences that make up all of creation, and so by invoking runes from each tradition at once, you can pull from the four corners of magic to unravel anything. You [invoke four runes](/Actions.aspx?ID=4265) of your choice, each of which must be from a different tradition of magic. In addition to the runes’ normal effects, one creature within 30 feet of all invoked runes must attempt a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude saving throw, taking 10d4 force damage on a failure as destructive magical reverberations clash in their body. If reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage or by the damage of any of the runes invoked, the creature’s body is torn apart into glowing script that describes the creature to the smallest detail, leaving no remains as the letters fade. The creature’s gear is unharmed.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Annihilating Swing](/Feats.aspx?ID=1240) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Extinction Curse</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Barbarian" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=18" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #156: The Apocalypse Prophet](/Sources.aspx?ID=36) pg. 72

</column>

---

You have learned from the brute destructive power of [xulgaths](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=102) and their kind. You make a melee Strike that ignores any resistances the target has. If you target a solid unattended object or surface with your Strike, you might automatically destroy it without an attack roll. If you target any object or surface with Hardness 20 or less that isn't a magic item or the effect of a spell, you destroy it. If the target object or surface is a magic item or the effect of a spell, you attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) it using your attack bonus with the Strike for the counteract check. On a successful counteract check, you destroy the object or surface unless it has Hardness greater than 20, is an artifact, or is similarly difficult to destroy. You destroy up to a 5-foot cube of an object or surface larger than Medium.
