<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Annotate Composition](/Feats.aspx?ID=1648) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Bard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=19" />
<trait label="Exploration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=66" />
<trait label="Linguistic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=101" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 113

</column>

---

By putting composition to paper, you can create a source of stirring words or song that others can read and understand. You spend 10 minutes and 1 Focus Point to transpose a composition spell on a special scroll that you or another creature can later activate. This composition spell must take a single action to cast. If the chosen composition spell requires a Performance check as part of the casting, the GM rolls this check as a secret check when you annotate your score. If you have [_inspire heroics_](/Spells.aspx?ID=388) or [_lingering composition_](/Spells.aspx?ID=389) and the chosen composition spell allows, you can also use one of those spells to modify the annotated composition, with the GM rolling the [secret](/Traits.aspx?ID=142) [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) check. If you do, you spend an additional Focus Point, even if the secret check fails.

 Any creature that can read the language you used when annotating your composition can Activate the Item by spending a single action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait. This produces the effects of the composition as though the activating creature had Cast the Spell.

 A composition you create this way loses its power the next time you make your daily preparations. While the composition is in your possession, you can render it inert using a single action that has the concentrate trait. You can't regain the Focus Points you spent to create the annotated composition until it is activated or loses its magic.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=645" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 126

**Archetype** [Infernal Pactbreaker](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=398)

**Prerequisites**
[Infernal Pactbreaker Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9488)

</column>

---

Many of the traps in the terms of a diabolic contract rely on curses, charms, or enchantments that enforce the behavior of the signatory. You’ve learned to draft amendments which nullify such effects, allowing others to walk free. You attempt to counteract a curse, a spell that alters how someone behaves such as _charm_, or the [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63), [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64) or [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=72) conditions. You use your choice of your Legal Lore or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) modifier as your [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=3280) modifier, and your counteract rank is equal to half your level rounded up. Regardless of the outcome, the target is then temporarily immune to your Annul Compulsion for 1 day.

Your swarm can emit a bright flash, much like aphet beetles, a genus of flash beetles once used by Osirian miners as sources of light. The swarm then glows with light like a [torch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2760) until it returns to your body

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs=""
>
[Apocalypse Rider Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7304) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Destiny" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=838" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 107

**Archetype** [Apocalypse Rider](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=287)

</column>

---

In the darkest hour of the night, a fearsome and terrible steed arrives as a gift from a powerful daemonic patron. You gain an apocalypse mount, which is loyal and follows your commands as long as you work to spread death and destruction. Your apocalypse mount can be any [mature animal companion](/Rules.aspx?ID=2117) with the [mount](/Feats.aspx?ID=2113) special ability, though it is obviously touched by daemonic forces. Choose whether your apocalypse mount is a [nimble](/Companions.aspx?Type=Advancement&ID=7) or [savage](/Companions.aspx?Type=Advancement&ID=8) animal companion. During an encounter, even if you don’t use the [Command an Animal](/Actions.aspx?ID=2400) action, your apocalypse mount can still use 1 action on your turn to [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) or [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306).

You also gain the anathema “You forswear any plans to cheat death or build something that will last beyond your own death.” If you break this anathema, you lose access to abilities granted by this archetype until you atone or make amends.

**Special** If you already have an animal companion with the mount special ability, it becomes your apocalypse mount as daemonic energies infuse its form. In such a case, one of your companion’s unarmed attacks increases one die size.

<title level="2">Apocalypse Rider Dedication leads to...</title>
[Behold, A Pale Horse](/Feats.aspx?ID=7305), [Contagious Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=7315), [Deathless Servant](/Feats.aspx?ID=7316), [History of Violence](/Feats.aspx?ID=7306), [Immortal Ruin](/Feats.aspx?ID=7319), [Jousting Mount](/Feats.aspx?ID=7307), [Memory of Nothing](/Feats.aspx?ID=7317), [Night Terror](/Feats.aspx?ID=7310), [One Among The Masses](/Feats.aspx?ID=7308), [Putrefaction](/Feats.aspx?ID=7309), [Soul Vessel Mount](/Feats.aspx?ID=7318), [Steal Death](/Feats.aspx?ID=7311), [To War!](/Feats.aspx?ID=7312), [Virulent Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=7313), [Wither Away](/Feats.aspx?ID=7314)

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 75 **Archetype** [Avenging Runelord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=338) **Frequency** Once per day **Prerequisites** [Avenging Runelord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8139) --- Your runelord may not have lived long enough to need to retreat into hiding in the face of Earthfall, but the apocalyptic echoes of this event nevertheless reached their soul all the way in the Boneyard. You’ve learned to endure the invasive thoughts of this empire-ending event, but now you can project that despair into the minds of others. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323) and target up to 10 creatures within 60 feet that you can sense. You force images into their minds of Earthfall, forcing them to endure a vision of the end of the world and all they hold dear. The creatures must attempt a Will save against your class DC or spell DC using mythic proficiency, whichever is higher. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is so distracted by the visions that they are [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 for 1 round.
**Failure** The creature is slowed 1 and [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 for 1 minute.
**Critical Failure** The creature is slowed 2 and stupefied 2 for 1 minute. In addition, the creature suffers the effects of the spell [_nightmare_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1615) the next time it rests. If the creature fails or critically fails against this effect, the effect repeats each time the creature attempts to sleep until it succeeds on its save or 6 days have passed. You do not need to know the creature’s name or remain on the same planet for the creature to experience these nightmares.

    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Apparition Cloud](/Feats.aspx?ID=7141) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Animist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=836" />
<trait label="Misfortune" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=654" />
<trait label="Wandering" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=843" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 26

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) After using Apparition Cloud, your familiar reincorporates at the start of your next turn and all effects of the feat end._

**Prerequisites**
[Spirit Familiar (Animist)](/Feats.aspx?ID=7123)

**Trigger**
You are targeted by an attack.

**Requirements**
Your familiar is adjacent to you or in your space.

</column>

---

With a mere thought, you discorporate your familiar into a thousand shards of spiritual magic, protecting both it and yourself from physical harm while making it difficult for enemies to move near you. You are [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) from the triggering attack. Until the start of your next turn, your familiar can’t be targeted and your enemies treat all spaces adjacent to you as [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366).

>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Animist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=836" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=579" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 22

</column>

---

You can see and interact with things others can’t. You have apparition sight, an imprecise sense that allows you to detect the presence of [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=83) or [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) [spirits](/Traits.aspx?ID=737), [haunts](/Traits.aspx?ID=622), and [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) within 30 feet of you.

You can allow a spirit or undead otherwise incapable of speech to speak through you as long as you are in direct contact with it. As an activity that takes 10 minutes, you can act as a link between disembodied souls and their mortal bodies. As long as you are in contact with both a spirit and a living body that belonged to it in life during that entire time, the spirit can use you to return to that body; this does not allow you to bring the dead back to life, but can assist in restoring a disembodied soul to a still-living body. If the body is occupied by another spirit or soul, that entity must succeed at a Will save against your spell DC or be cast from the body when its original owner is returned.

[Spirit Walk](/Feats.aspx?ID=7137)

    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Arc of Destruction](/Feats.aspx?ID=7290) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 83

**Trigger**
An enemy you’re observing targets you with a ranged weapon [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306).

</column>

---

You redirect an incoming weapon or projectile and send your enemy’s own attack roaring back at them, increasing its accuracy with a surge of mythic power. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320); you gain a +4 status bonus to AC against the triggering Strike. If the Strike fails, you immediately snatch the weapon or ammunition used for the attack out of the air and launch it back at the enemy, using mythic proficiency for your Strike. If the attack was made with a [thrown](/Traits.aspx?ID=711) weapon, add the weapon’s [runes](/Rules.aspx?ID=3162) and other effects to the attack as normal. If the triggering attack was made with a piece of ammunition that you’re wielding an appropriate weapon for, you can apply your weapon’s runes and other effects to the attack.

</title>

<traits>

</column>

---

Your arcane legacy grants you an exceptional aptitude for intellectual and academic pursuits. You become trained in one skill of your choice. Additionally, you keep a book of arcane spells similar to a wizard’s spellbook. You add all the spells in your spell repertoire to this book for free, and you can add additional arcane spells to the book by paying the appropriate cost and using your Arcana skill, similarly to how a wizard can Learn Spells to add those spells to his spellbook.

 During your daily preparations, choose any one spell from your book of arcane spells. If it isn’t in your spell repertoire, add it to your spell repertoire until the next time you prepare. If it’s already in your spell repertoire, add it as an additional signature spell for that day.

<title level="2">Arcane Evolution leads to...</title>
[Greater Mental Evolution](/Feats.aspx?ID=626), [Greater Physical Evolution](/Feats.aspx?ID=1825)

---

Your physical training encompasses unarmed combat forms. The damage die for your [fist](/Weapons.aspx?ID=1) changes to 1d6 instead of 1d4. You don't take the normal –2 circumstance penalty when making a lethal attack with your fist or any other [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attacks. Your unarmed attacks gain the [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11) trait, making them [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103). At 5th level, you also gain the [critical specialization effects](/Rules.aspx?ID=235) of unarmed attacks in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group and weapons in the brawling group, and the critical specialization effect uses your spell DC instead of your class DC.

</title>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Archetype** [Edgewatch Detective](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=85)

</column>

---

You can sense the presence of the supernatural, even if you don't have any magical ability yourself. You can spend a single action (this action has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait) to determine if any magical auras are present in the area. This has the effects of a 1st-level [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=66) spell but isn't magical. By straining, you can also discover the source of the magic and its school (with the effect of a 4th-level _detect magic_ spell), but doing so prevents you from using this ability again until you've rested for 8 hours.

**Prerequisites**

**Requirements**

---

Your magic has a powerful aftereffect, briefly granting you a certain spell. When you take this feat, choose three of [_false vitality_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1523), [_fire shield_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1529), [_fleet step_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1531), [_flicker_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1532), [_invisibility_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1577), [_mountain resilience_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1610), and [_see the unseen_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1663). You use [Arcane Cascade](/Actions.aspx?ID=756) and are subject to an additional aftereffect spell of your choice from the three you selected. This aftereffect spell’s duration lasts until the end of your next turn or its normal duration, whichever is shorter. Using Arcane Shroud again ends any existing spell you gained from Arcane Shroud.

Your magic has a powerful aftereffect, briefly granting you a certain spell. When you take this feat, choose three of [_false vitality_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1523), [_fleet step_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1531), [_invisibility_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1577), [_mountain resilience_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1610), [_resist energy_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1651), and [_see the unseen_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1663). 

When you use [Arcane Cascade](/Actions.aspx?ID=756), choose one of the spells you selected with this feat. You’re affected by this aftereffect spell until the end of your next turn, though it ends early if the stance ends or another circumstance ends it (such as if you take a [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=2251) while affected by _invisibility_). If you’re 18th level or higher, a _false vitality_ or _resist energy_ you get from Arcane Shroud is heightened to 4th rank.

**Special** You can select this feat a second time to add the remaining spells to your set of choices.

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 41 **Prerequisites** [Warrior Automaton](/Heritages.aspx?ID=187) heritage **Requirements** You have a creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=33). --- You channel magical power from your core into your arm, empowering your attack as you attempt to slam your foe into the ground. Attempt an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check against the foe's Fortitude DC. You take a –2 circumstance penalty to your check if the target is one size larger than you and a –4 circumstance penalty if it's larger than that. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your check if the target is one size smaller than you and a +4 circumstance bonus if it's smaller than that. **Critical Success** You slam the foe down and the magical energy overwhelms it. The creature is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31), becomes [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) for 1 round, and takes damage equal to 2d6 plus your Strength modifier. The foe is no longer grabbed or restrained by you.
**Success** You slam the foe down. The creature is knocked prone and takes damage equal to your Strength modifier. The foe is no longer grabbed or restrained by you.
**Failure** You are unable to slam the creature, but your hold on the creature remains.
**Critical Failure** The creature breaks free and is no longer grabbed or restrained by you. **Enhancement** Your arms better channel your core's power. You no longer take penalties for attempting to slam larger foes. Your foe takes damage equal to 2d6 plus your Strength modifier on a success (or double that on a critical success).

You become trained in all simple and martial weapons in the [bow](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=3) weapon group. Whenever you gain a class feature that grants you expert or greater proficiency in certain weapons, you also gain that proficiency rank in all simple and martial weapons in the bow weapon group. If you are at least an expert in the bow you are using, you gain access to the critical specialization effect with that bow.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the archer archetype.

<title level="2">Archer Dedication leads to...</title>
[Advanced Bow Training](/Feats.aspx?ID=1887), [Archer's Aim](/Feats.aspx?ID=1889), [Crossbow Terror](/Feats.aspx?ID=1888), [Quick Shot](/Feats.aspx?ID=1886), [Staggering Fire](/Feats.aspx?ID=3616)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs=""
>
[Archfiend Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7320) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Destiny" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=838" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 110

**Archetype** [Archfiend](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=288)

</column>

---

Driven by your Calling, you've begun to make plans for your own personal realm from whence you're destined to rule over an army of fiends. Name your realm and describe its eventual appearance. Whether it contains raging hellfire, ponds of caustic acid, or banks of poisonous fog, your realm should be marked by distinctive [terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=3108). Select one of the following damage types associated with your realm's environmental dangers: [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524), [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), or [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669). This is your realm's damage type. You gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) to the selected damage type equal to half your level. If you already have resistance to this damage type, increase your resistance by 5. The certainty of your will is such that you can temporarily bring forth a portion of your realm into this world. You gain the Manifest Realm ability. Other feats allow you to further manipulate your manifested realm. 

Manifest Realm <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Effect** You corrupt the surrounding area into a manifestation of your realm in a 20-foot-radius burst centered on you. Your manifested realm counts as [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) for your enemies, and your enemies take a –1 penalty to Fortitude saving throws while in your manifested realm. You can Sustain your manifested realm once per round on subsequent rounds, and if you do not, the radius of your manifested realm is reduced by 5 feet. Your realm remains manifested for a maximum of 1 minute, and you can Dismiss your manifested realm. If your manifested realm's radius is ever reduced to 0 feet or if you move beyond 100 feet from the borders of your manifested realm, your manifested realm is automatically Dismissed.

<title level="2">Archfiend Dedication leads to...</title>
[Brandish Authority](/Feats.aspx?ID=7327), [Don thy Fervor](/Feats.aspx?ID=7321), [Fiend Eternal](/Feats.aspx?ID=7330), [Imprison Foe](/Feats.aspx?ID=7328), [Lord of the Fiends](/Feats.aspx?ID=7322), [Manipulate Realm](/Feats.aspx?ID=7323), [Marshall Fiendish Forces](/Feats.aspx?ID=7324), [Profane Bargain](/Feats.aspx?ID=7329), [Realm Strider](/Feats.aspx?ID=7325), [Seat of Power](/Feats.aspx?ID=7326)

Flames rise and shape to your will, forming a wall or dome of your design. You create a [_wall of fire_](/Spells.aspx?ID=362) within 120 feet. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 24

**Archetype** [Hellknight](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=372)

**Prerequisites**
[Hellknight Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8812)

</column>

---

You've trained to resist the manipulations of [fiends](/Traits.aspx?ID=600), and your Hellknight discipline makes you difficult to influence. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saves against effects that could inflict the [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64) or [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) conditions.

 If a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effect would compel you to act in a way that violates your Hellknight order's tenets (as determined by the GM), you can attempt to break free from the effect as a free action triggered by receiving the violating order, and you gain a new Will save against the effect. You can attempt this save even if the effect would normally prevent you from acting of your own volition. You can attempt this new save only once for a given effect, even if you're compelled to violate your order's tenets multiple times. You can't receive a worse result on this Will save than you originally got against the compelling mental effect.

**Source** [Pathfinder #223: Hell's Destiny](/Sources.aspx?ID=336) pg. 223 **Archetype** [Chelaxian Scion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=384) **Prerequisites** [Chelaxian Scion Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8971) --- Through consistent (and often punishing) practice, you’ve learned how to use your house’s preferred weapons. You have familiarity with either one martial weapon of your choice; two simple or martial weapons of your choice from your house’s preferred weapons list; or one advanced weapon of your choice from your house’s preferred weapons list. For the purpose of proficiency, treat any of these selections that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons. If you’re at least an expert in one of the selected weapons, you get the critical specialization effect of that weapon when you get a critical hit with it. **Charthagnion**: Weapons with the [disarm](/Traits.aspx?ID=577) or [parry](/Traits.aspx?ID=667) trait
**Elliendo**: [Brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) weapons and [knives](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=9)
**Henderthane**: [Hammers](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=8) and [picks](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=10)
**Jeggare**: One-handed [swords](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=15)
**Leroung**: [Clubs](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=5) and [shields](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=12)
**Narikopolus**: [Bows](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=3)
**Sarini**: [Flails](/Weapons.aspx?ID=374)
**Thrune**: [Clubs](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=5) and [crossbows](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=17) In addition, you gain the For My House! action. **For My House!** **Frequency** once per minute; **Effect** You announce your house affiliation, either by declaring it aloud (giving this ability the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) trait) or openly displaying your house heraldry (giving this ability the [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727) trait). Until the beginning of your next turn, your weapon Strikes and spells deal an additional 1 damage to any creature that witnessed the display. If you’re an expert in [Cheliax Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41), Genealogy Lore, Heraldry Lore, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45), or Warfare Lore, the additional damage increases to 2. The damage increases to 3 if you’re a master in the skill or 4 if you’re legendary in the skill.

</column>

---

Add the following property runes to the list you can choose for your blessed armament: animated, [_greater fearsome_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2837), [_grievous_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2841), [_keen_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2843), and [_greater vitalizing_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2852). If you have the Radiant Armament feat, add [_greater astral_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2832) and [_greater brilliant_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2833) to the list as well. In addition, you can change the rune you've selected for the day to a different rune from your list as a single action that has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) and [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579) traits. Changing the rune doesn't restore abilities that can be used only a limited number of times.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

**Prerequisites**

</column>

---

You've learned to wear the iconic Hellknight armor. You become trained in light armor and [Hellknight breastplate](/Armor.aspx?ID=23), a medium armor. If you were already trained in light armor and medium armor, you gain training in [Hellknight half plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=24) and [Hellknight plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=25). Whenever you gain a class feature that grants you expert or greater proficiency in any type of armor (but not unarmored defense), you also gain that proficiency in the armor types granted to you by this feat. If you have a class feature that grants you expert proficiency in unarmored defense and you're 13th level or higher, you also become an expert in the armor types granted to you by this feat.

 In addition, when you choose this feat, you receive a non-magical suit of Hellknight armor of a type you become trained in (Hellknight breastplate, Hellknight half plate, or Hellknight plate).

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 203

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) The DCs for the Armor Assist feat are not subject to GM adjudication. Rather, simply use the default DCs listed in the feat: 15 for common armor, 20 for uncommon armor, and 25 for rare armor._

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) or Trained in [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8)

</column>

---

After your service aiding armored combatants, you are practiced in helping yourself and others don heavy gear. You can attempt an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) or [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) check with a DC determined by the GM (but usually 15 for common armor, DC 20 for uncommon armor, and DC 25 for rare armor) to halve the time you take to don armor. You can halve an ally's time to don armor by working with them to don the armor and succeeding at an Athletics or Warfare Lore check against the same DC.

    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Armor Break](/Feats.aspx?ID=7867) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Guardian" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=859" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 46

**Requirements**
You are wearing medium or heavy armor that doesn’t have the broken condition, and your current Hit Points are at half your maximum or lower.

</column>

---

You flex your muscles to crack your damaged armor, blasting jagged shards into nearby enemies. Each enemy in a 10-foot  [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) takes 11d6 piercing damage with a Reflex save against your class DC. You can [push](/Rules.aspx?ID=2364) any enemy that fails its save 5 feet away from you (or up to 10 feet on a critical failure). The damage increases by 1d6 per level beyond 14th. Your armor gains the [broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=60) condition. While your armor remains broken due to Armor Break, you don't take its penalty to Speed. In addition, if the broken armor has the [bulwark](/Traits.aspx?ID=549) trait, you retain its bonus to Reflex saves, but the bonus is reduced by 1.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Earth" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=55" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 26

</column>

---

Stone encases you like armor. The stone armor is medium armor but uses your highest armor proficiency. The stone armor's statistics are: _AC Bonus_ +4; Dex Cap +1; _Check Penalty_ –2; _Speed Penalty_ –10 feet; _Strength_ +3; _Bulk_ 1; _Group_ [plate](/ArmorGroups.aspx?ID=4). You gain its [armor specialization effect](/Rules.aspx?ID=211). Any bonuses, runes, and magical abilities of your actual armor are suppressed, but any runes that could apply to the stone armor are replicated onto it. The stone armor lasts for 10 minutes, and you can Dismiss this impulse. If you use this impulse again, any existing one ends.

---
**Level (3rd)** The armor becomes heavy armor. Its AC Bonus becomes +5, and it gains the [bulwark](/Traits.aspx?ID=202) armor trait.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Armor Rune Shifter](/Feats.aspx?ID=1149) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #148: Fires of the Haunted City](/Sources.aspx?ID=13) pg. 75

**Archetype** [Crystal Keeper](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=34)

**Prerequisites**
[Crystal Keeper Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1146)

</column>

---

You learn the secrets of armor runes by viewing them through gems and can alter them at your discretion. Once per day when you make your daily preparations, you can focus on a rune’s magical energies through a crystal’s facets to alter a single property rune on one suit of armor in your possession to suppress its normal effects and make it function as a different property rune. You can temporarily alter the rune to function as one of the following runes: [_energy-resistant_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=283), [_fortification_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=285), [_glamered_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=286), [_invisibility_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=287), [_shadow_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=288), or [_slick_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=289). The property rune remains altered until you make your next daily preparations. The armor must meet the prerequisites for the temporary rune, and any other runes that required the suppressed rune are also suppressed while the rune is transformed. The rune is obviously altered, and thus the armor can’t be sold as though it had the temporary rune.

fields.text: Feat 10 Armor Rune Shifter Archetype Source Pathfinder #148: Fires of the Haunted City pg. 75 Archetype Crystal Keeper Prerequisites Crystal Keeper Dedication You learn the secrets of armor runes by viewing them through gems and can alter them at your discretion. Once per day when you make your daily preparations, you can focus on a rune’s magical energies through a crystal’s facets to alter a single property rune on one suit of armor in your possession to suppress its normal effects and make it function as a different property rune. You can temporarily alter the rune to function as one of the following runes: energy-resistant , fortification , glamered , invisibility , shadow , or slick . The property rune remains altered until you make your next daily preparations. The armor must meet the prerequisites for the temporary rune, and any other runes that required the suppressed rune are also suppressed while the rune is transformed. The rune is obviously altered, and thus the armor can’t be sold as though it had the temporary rune.

You have learned techniques to adjust and modify your armor and movements to reduce the noise you make. When you wear non-[noisy](/Traits.aspx?ID=205) armor with which you are trained, your penalty to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks is reduced by 1 (to a minimum penalty of 0). If you're a master in Stealth, reduce the penalty by 2, and if you're legendary, reduce the penalty by 3. If your armor has the noisy trait, instead of reducing the penalty to Stealth checks, you ignore the effects of the noisy trait, enabling you to remove the penalty with a sufficient Strength score as normal.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=606" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 116

**Archetype** [Ascended Celestial](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=289)

**Prerequisites**
[Ascended Celestial Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7331)

**Requirements**
Your nimbus is active.

</column>

---

Even alone, you’re a force to be reckoned with— an army of one, so long as you have your celestial armaments. Spend 1 Mythic Point. If you’re not currently wielding your celestial armament, it immediately teleports into your hand. With a gesture and a whispered prayer, you launch your celestial armament into the air, where it flies with a mind of its own, attacking every enemy within your nimbus. Make a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with that weapon against each enemy in the [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2402) of your nimbus. Each attack counts toward your multiple attack penalty, but your penalty doesn’t increase until you have made all your attacks. After these attacks are complete, your weapon returns to your hand.

</title>

<traits>

**Archetype** [Artillerist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=115)

**Prerequisites**
trained in martial weapons

</column>

---

Artillery is a team sport, where every member of the crew has to rely on the other members. At best, a mistake might just waste time. At worst, a misaligned fuse or a badly set pin could cause the whole thing to explode. You've taken these lessons to heart, and so your presence on an artillery team assists the entire team at every aspect of the [siege weapon's](/SiegeWeapons.aspx) deployment and usage. If you're serving on a siege weapon crew, you and all other members gain a +2 circumstance bonus to any checks to [Load](/Rules.aspx?ID=1625), [Aim](/Rules.aspx?ID=1624), move, or [Repair](/Actions.aspx?ID=42) the weapon. When you Aim a siege weapon, you can move the weapon's aim twice as far as normal.

<title level="2">Artillerist Dedication leads to...</title>
[Cannon Corner Shot](/Feats.aspx?ID=3225), [Live Ammunition](/Feats.aspx?ID=3227), [Master Siege Engineer](/Feats.aspx?ID=3228), [Shorthanded](/Feats.aspx?ID=3224)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Artokus's Fire](/Feats.aspx?ID=2158) <actions string="Free Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Additive 2" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=4" />
<trait label="Alchemist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=7" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Legends](/Sources.aspx?ID=40) pg. 20

**Frequency**
once per round

**Trigger**
You use [Quick Alchemy](/Actions.aspx?ID=2) to craft an [alchemist's fire](/Equipment.aspx?ID=75), and that bomb's level is at least 2 levels lower than your advanced alchemy level.

</column>

---

Artokus developed a mixture of volatile materials that burns hotter and longer than typical alchemist's fire. You include this additive mixture when crafting your alchemist's fire. The alchemist's fire deals 1d4 [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) in addition to what the alchemist fire would normally cause (for instance, a moderate alchemist's fire deals 1d4+2 persistent fire damage). A creature taking persistent fire damage from the alchemist's fire requires two successful flat checks to end the persistent damage, or one check if the creature had an assisted recovery that reduces the flat check to DC 10. The enhanced alchemist's fire burns even underwater, and any attempts to end the persistent damage by using water have no effect.

<title level="2">Artokus's Discoveries</title>

**Source** [Legends](/Sources.aspx?ID=40) pg. 20

Artokus Kirran's legacy includes far more than just the sun orchid elixir. As one of the longest-lived alchemists in Golarion, he's developed a number of other significant alchemical discoveries known across the Inner Sea region. The following are some of his more notable discoveries. Artokus is cautious about sharing his alchemical techniques and typically only does so with his most trusted students.

**Related Feats**: [Wish Alchemy](/Feats.aspx?ID=2159)

Though you may have stolen from the hive, you’ve nothing but respect for the armies guarding it, and you borrow their strength to overwhelm your foes. Your body transforms into a swarm of bees. You [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) up to twice your Speed; during this movement you can pass through any space that would be small enough for a single insect, and your movement does not trigger reactions. If you pass through an enemy’s space, you can inflict a storm of stings that deals 3d4 piercing damage and 3d4 poison damage, with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save against your class DC. At the end of your movement, you return to your original form. At 10th level and every two levels thereafter, the damage increases by 1d4 piercing damage and 1d4 poison damage.

<title

    right="Feat 1"

[As in Life, So in Death](/Feats.aspx?ID=3532) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Skeleton" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=236" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 56

</column>

---

Specific memories of your old life are hard to hold onto, but you know things without remembering why. You gain the [Adopted Ancestry](/Feats.aspx?ID=751) feat. You can choose any ancestry, but it is likely to be one that matches both your skeleton heritage and who you were in life. As long as your body is completely covered by armor or clothing, you do not have to attempt [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks against a creature's Perception DC to successfully [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) yourself as a member of that ancestry. This is a non-magical disguise that doesn't protect against divination. This disguise doesn't provide any benefit against a creature actively attempting a Perception check against you.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Hell's Destiny</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=615" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=695" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #223: Hell's Destiny](/Sources.aspx?ID=336) pg. 231

**Prerequisites**
Master in [Games Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41)

</column>

---

You’re a master of strategy games, able to translate strategies and mechanics from these games to the actual battles they were created to simulate. You can use your proficiency rank in [Games Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) for anything that requires proficiency in Warfare Lore (such as prerequisites) and use your Games Lore modifier in place of your Warfare Lore modifier for checks. You can use Games Lore to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) on military professionals, such as mercenaries and commanders. Your reputation as a strategist opens up opportunities while you’re in a military camp, near a battlefield, or somewhere else that has numerous non‑hostile soldiers, allowing you to [Earn Income](/Actions.aspx?ID=2364) with Games Lore with a task level of at least your level – 1. 

If you [lead a troop](/Rules.aspx?ID=3439) and have had time to create a [skirmish bond](/Rules.aspx?ID=3452) with them, you’ve also spent time going over the finer points of strategy and even played against many members of your troop. Once per day, you can roll Games Lore for initiative when leading this troop.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 115

**Archetype** [Ascended Celestial](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=289)

**Prerequisites**

</column>

---

As you strive to ascend to the ranks of celestials, the pull of gravity loosens on your body. You gain a [fly Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2350) equal to your land Speed and the Flyby Attack action. When you gain this feat, you can choose to sprout wings, if desired; these wings are permanent. 

Once per day as a single action, you can fly at incredible speeds. When you do, your fly Speed becomes equal to double your Speed for 5 rounds.

**Flyby Attack** <actions string="Two Actions" /> **Effect** You Fly and can make a Strike at any point along the way.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Dragonblood" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=794" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Draconic Codex](/Sources.aspx?ID=277) pg. 217

**Prerequisites**
[draconic exemplar](/DraconicBenefactors.aspx) associated with a specific plane (such as a [diabolic dragon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=398) or [empyreal dragon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=399))

</column>

---

Twice per week, you can cast [_interplanar teleport_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1576) as an [innate](/Rules.aspx?ID=2901) spell of the tradition corresponding to your draconic exemplar. This can be used only to travel to the plane associated with your draconic exemplar (for instance, [Heaven](/Planes.aspx?ID=41) if your draconic nature is tied to an empyreal dragon) or from that plane to [the Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=26). Due to your draconic blood, your body serves as the locus, and you don’t require a planar key. If there’s any question about the plane to which your draconic exemplar is associated, the GM determines the answer.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs=""
>
[Ascended Celestial Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7331) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Destiny" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=838" />
<trait label="Fortune" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=612" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 115

**Archetype** [Ascended Celestial](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=289)

</column>

---

Your Calling has driven you to perform mortal deeds that will result in your ascension to the ranks of celestials. You’re headstrong and determined and hardly waver in your resolve; once per hour, you can roll twice and use the higher result on a Will saving throw. If you ever become [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63), rather than attack wildly, you become stubbornly immobile, wasting all your actions until the condition ends. 

Additionally, you emanate a nimbus of light. You shed [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2402) in a 30-foot radius (and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2403) to the next 30 feet). You can suppress or reestablish this light as a single action that has the concentrate trait. As long as your nimbus is active, all allies in the area of your nimbus gain a +1 status bonus to saves against fear. You gain the Bless Ally action.

**Bless Ally** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612), [mythic](/Traits.aspx?ID=835)) **Frequency** once per 10 minutes; **Requirements** Your nimbus is active; **Target** a willing ally within the bright light of your nimbus; **Effect** Your radiance grants an ally some of your celestial grace. That ally can roll twice and use the higher result for the next Will save they attempt before the beginning of your next turn.

<title level="2">Ascended Celestial Dedication leads to...</title>
[A Thousand Cries For Help](/Feats.aspx?ID=7337), [Abjure Harm](/Feats.aspx?ID=7336), [Aegis for the Innocent](/Feats.aspx?ID=7332), [Army of One](/Feats.aspx?ID=7340), [Ascend](/Feats.aspx?ID=7333), [Celestial Armaments](/Feats.aspx?ID=7338), [Celestial Rebirth](/Feats.aspx?ID=7344), [Channel Divine Spark](/Feats.aspx?ID=7335), [Cleansing Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=7339), [Consult Celestial Advisor](/Feats.aspx?ID=7334), [Eyes Unclouded](/Feats.aspx?ID=7341), [Shining Glory](/Feats.aspx?ID=7342)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 158

**Archetype** [Assassin](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=48)

**Prerequisites**
[Alchemical Crafting](/Feats.aspx?ID=752); Trained in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4); Trained in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5); Trained in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15)

</column>

---

You've trained to assassinate your foes, and you do so with tenacity and precision. You gain the Mark for Death activity.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> Mark for Death;    **Requirements** You can see and hear the creature you intend to mark; **Effect** You designate a single creature as your mark. This lasts until the mark dies or you use Mark for Death again. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) your mark and on [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks to [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=48) against your mark. Your [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170) and [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179) weapons and [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attacks gain the [backstabber](/Traits.aspx?ID=172) and [deadly d6](/Traits.aspx?ID=174) weapon traits when you're attacking your mark. If the weapon or unarmed attack already has the deadly trait, increase the size of the deadly damage die by one step instead of giving it deadly d6.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you've gained two other feats from the assassin archetype.

<title level="2">Assassin Dedication leads to...</title>
[Angel of Death](/Feats.aspx?ID=1893), [Angel of Vindication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3612), [Assassinate](/Feats.aspx?ID=1894), [Eclipsed Vitality](/Feats.aspx?ID=3613), [Expert Backstabber](/Feats.aspx?ID=1891), [Public Execution](/Feats.aspx?ID=4143), [Surprise Attack](/Feats.aspx?ID=1892)

 ** Mark for Death** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Requirements** The creature you intend to mark is [observed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=84) by you; **Effect** You designate a single creature as your mark. You can Dismiss this impulse. You become Large if you were smaller. This increases your reach by 5 feet (or by 10 feet if you started out Tiny). You gain a climb Speed equal to your land Speed, but you can use it only to climb surfaces of earthen matter. The armor grants you a +1 circumstance bonus to your Fortitude saves and a +2 circumstance bonus to your Fortitude or Reflex DCs against attempts to Shove you, Trip you, or knock you prone. If your Strength is below +4, this armor raises your Strength to +4. If your Strength is +4 or higher, this armor grants you a +1 item bonus to your Strength. >
[Assume Godhood](/Feats.aspx?ID=7402) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 133

**Archetype** [Godling](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=293)

**Prerequisites**
[Godling Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7392)

</column>

---

You complete your apotheosis into living godhood, allowing you to empower more followers. You can serve as the [deity](/Rules.aspx?ID=2048) for classes with a deity feature, such as clerics, empowering them to cast divine spells with their class features. When you serve as the deity in this way, you can provide any aspect of a deity stat block (such as domains or a favored weapon) that you yourself have acquired from a godling feat. In addition, you can choose one skill you are legendary in to act as your divine skill, and your divine attributes include your key attribute and one other attribute of your choosing.

When you Assume Godhood, choose three spells from any list other than the [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) list; one must be 1st rank, one must be 2nd or 3rd rank, and one can be of any rank. These spells become additional cleric spells you can grant to your followers. You gain the Intercession Spell ability, allowing you to directly provide the magic that your hierophant uses to enact your miracles.  

**Intercession Spell** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [spellshape](/Traits.aspx?ID=513)) **Frequency** once per day **Trigger** Your hierophant Casts a Spell; **Effect** Interceding directly in your hierophant's affairs, you grant them additional magic. They do not expend the spell slot, usage, or Focus Point.

If you die after Assuming Godhood, only your mortal body perishes, and you continue your existence as a deity, watching over the Universe from afar. In this deific form, you cannot move, act, or speak normally, though you still grant spells to your followers and can perceive and affect them using your godling abilities like Receive Prayers or Intercession Spell, regardless of range. If you need to take more direct action in creation, you can descend to the Universe and incarnate yourself into a mortal body of your choosing within 1 mile of one of your followers or a holy site relevant to your faith, which has the same statistics and abilities that you had before you died. This new body can have any appearance you wish, but typically retains at least one feature important to your divine iconography, such as eye color, a scar, or a unique birthmark. You can incarnate yourself as often as you like, but repeated direct intercessions in the affairs of mortals typically attract the attention and sanction of older and more established deities.

Even in the worst circumstances, you can perform basic tasks. Choose a skill you're trained in. You can forgo rolling a skill check for that skill to instead receive a result of 10 + your proficiency bonus (do not apply any other bonuses, penalties, or modifiers).<details class="clarification"><details-summary> Paizo Clarification</details-summary>What happens to abilities that depend on your roll when you set your die to a certain result instead of actually rolling? Typically, it still counts as a roll for abilities that trigger off your roll.

For example, if you used Assurance to automatically get a result of 10 + your proficiency bonus and it would be a success, an ability that applies to that skill and says “when you roll a success, you get a critical success instead” would still upgrade your result to a critical success. Though this general rule should apply most of the time, a GM might rule otherwise in certain circumstances based on the specific abilities and their themes.</details>

**Special** You can select this feat multiple times. Each time, choose a different skill and gain the benefits for that skill.

    right="Feat 13"

>
[Astral Blink](/Feats.aspx?ID=3106) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Automaton" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=398" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 42

</column>

---

You've attuned your core to allow you to phase in and out of the [Astral Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=8), allowing you to teleport periodically. You can cast [_dimension door_](/Spells.aspx?ID=69) once per hour as a 4th-level innate arcane spell.

**Enhancement** Your attunement allows you to teleport in a series of quick jumps rather than in one big leap. You can expend your hourly use of _dimension door_ as a free action when you begin your turn. If you do, your Strides are augmented until the end of your turn, allowing you to instantly teleport to any point you could reach with your Speed instead of traversing normally to the location. While augmented, your Strides gain the [conjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=33) and [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=156) traits. Your augmented Strides don't trigger reactions that can be triggered by [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114) actions or upon leaving or entering a square, unless those reactions trigger on teleportation.

<title

    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Astral Tether](/Feats.aspx?ID=3663) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
<trait label="Psychic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=430" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 24

</column>

---

You spin out a thread of psychic energy that connects you to an ally, using it as a conduit for your abilities. Choose a willing creature within 60 feet and connect to it. Whenever you would gain a benefit from a psychic amp, you can have the amp affect the tethered creature instead. You can do so only if the amp grants a distinct benefit, not if it alters the amped spell. 

The tether can't be severed physically but breaks if the distance between you and the tethered ally ever exceeds 60 feet, if you become [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38), or if you use Astral Tether again.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Athletic Strategist](/Feats.aspx?ID=1452) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Investigator" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=318" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 60

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3)

</column>

---

You know how to calculatedly manipulate joints and body weight. In addition to using [Devise a Stratagem](/Actions.aspx?ID=546) to modify a Strike, you can use it to modify a [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=41), [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=35), [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=38), or [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40) attempt, substituting your Devise a Stratagem roll for the [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check. You must apply the substitution to the first eligible attack you make, whether it's a Strike or one of the Athletics actions.

 You can also use your Intelligence modifier instead of Strength for the Athletics check when you substitute your Devise a Stratagem roll, unless you're using a weapon for the maneuver and the weapon doesn't fit the restrictions for using Intelligence with a stratagem.

<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=389" />

</traits>

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 45, [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 90, [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 91

**Archetypes** [Marshal](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=66) (Level 8), [Marshal](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=254) (Level 8), [Golden Legionnaire](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=373) (Level 8)

**Trigger**
A creature within your reach uses a manipulate action or a move action, makes a ranged attack, or leaves a square during a move action it’s using.

</column>

---

You lash out at a foe that leaves an opening. Make a melee Strike against the triggering creature. If your attack is a critical hit and the trigger was a [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104) action, you disrupt that action. This Strike doesn’t count toward your multiple attack penalty, and your multiple attack penalty doesn’t apply to this Strike.

<title level="2">Attack of Opportunity leads to...</title>
[Disorienting Opening](/Feats.aspx?ID=1727), [Impassable Wall Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=1091)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Attunement Shift](/Feats.aspx?ID=2996) <actions string="Free Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 212

**Archetype** [Geomancer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=100)

**Frequency**
once per 10 minutes

**Prerequisites**
[Geomancer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2995)

**Requirements**
Your previous action was to cast a spell with the [air](/Traits.aspx?ID=5), [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27), [earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125), or [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165) trait.

</column>

---

The magic of your spell floods into you, overriding your connection to the land around you. You alter your terrain attunement to a terrain that matches a trait of the spell you just cast. You thereby gain your terrain attunement benefit when you cast further spells with the same descriptor, instead of using the terrain you're actually in. For instance, if you cast [_tanglefoot_](/Spells.aspx?ID=330), your terrain attunement switches to your choice of forest or swamp, and your terrain attunement applies when you cast another plant spell.

 Your terrain attunement reverts to that of the terrain you're in 1 minute after you use Attunement Shift.

---

Your presence as an avatar of evil makes your foes more susceptible to terror and makes it almost impossible for them to shake off fear when you are near. Enemies within 15 feet of you take a –1 circumstance penalty to saving throws against [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68). In addition, an enemy that ends its turn within 15 feet of you can't reduce the value of its [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) condition below 1.

    right="Feat 20"
    pfs="Limited"
>

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Age of Ashes</spoilers>

<traits>

**Prerequisites**

</column>

---

You are a paragon of all that is good, your overwhelming aura causing evildoers to cower. All evil creatures within 15 feet of you take a –1 status penalty to checks and DCs that target you or your allies. This penalty is –2 against creatures you have taken an oath against (such as dragons if you have the [Dragonslayer Oath](/Feats.aspx?ID=219) feat). You can choose to suppress or resume this aura as an action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait.

<title level="2">Paragons of Promise</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #150: Broken Promises](/Sources.aspx?ID=15) pg. 75

The citizens of Promise represent some of the most capable experts, greatest minds, and powerful warriors on Golarion—ideal teachers and trainers for PCs who want to maximize their own potential. If the PCs secure Visitor’s Pins or an alliance with Mengkare, their access to Promise’s trainers and records unlock all of the following uncommon class feats.

**Related Feats**: [Apex Companion](/Feats.aspx?ID=1160), [Bloodline Metamorphosis](/Feats.aspx?ID=1162), [Efficient Alchemy (Paragon)](/Feats.aspx?ID=1163), [Emblazon Divinity](/Feats.aspx?ID=1164), [Enduring Debilitation](/Feats.aspx?ID=1165), [Golden Body](/Feats.aspx?ID=1166), [Song of the Fallen](/Feats.aspx?ID=1168), [Spell Mastery](/Feats.aspx?ID=1843), [Superior Sight](/Feats.aspx?ID=1170), [Ultimate Flexibility](/Feats.aspx?ID=1732), [Unstoppable Juggernaut](/Feats.aspx?ID=1631)

You choose the size when you Channel Elements and can change it when you use a stance impulse that affects your kinetic aura. Increase the maximum size you can choose by 5 feet at 15th and 20th levels.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 78 **Frequency** once per hour **Prerequisites** Expert in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) --- You've learned how to read the natural auras of other living creatures. To do this, you must focus on a single living target without blinking for 1 minute. You can do this while performing some other minor task—such as making conversation to distract from your intentions—but you can't blink or otherwise lose your concentration. You can then perceive any or all of the following information.
  • The target's current apparent attitude toward you ([friendly](/Conditions.aspx?ID=18), [indifferent](/Conditions.aspx?ID=25), and so on).
  • The target's current apparent emotional state.
  • A general assessment of the target's physical health, such as what conditions or afflictions it has. You might need to succeed at an Occultism check against the affliction or condition's DC to detect the presence of a specifically hidden or subtle condition or affliction.
In addition, the GM rolls a secret Occultism check for you against the target's [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) DC. If your result exceeds your target's, you can identify if they're being deceptive in some way (such as expressing a false attitude toward you or faking an emotional state). This doesn't allow you to automatically identify the exact nature of that deception, only to tell the outward appearance is false.

>
[Aurochs-Headed](/Feats.aspx?ID=7648) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Triumph of the Tusk</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #207: Resurrection Flood](/Sources.aspx?ID=249) pg. 80

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) or Trained in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40)

</column>

---

Your words and body language can subconsciously unsettle orcs, giving you an advantage when convincing them to see things your way. Many with this feat use it to travel freely between holds, warning all but the toughest orcs to waylay weaker prey. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to skill checks to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) or [Coerce](/Actions.aspx?ID=2394) creatures with the orc trait. Enemy [orcs](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=66) who can see you at the start of combat take a –1 penalty to initiative rolls.

</title>

**Prerequisites**
[divine ally (steed)](/Classes.aspx?ID=4); [Imposing Destrier](/Feats.aspx?ID=238)

</column>

---

Guided by your ongoing care, your steed has developed incredible intelligence and skill. The mount you gained through the divine ally class feature is now a [specialized animal companion](/Rules.aspx?ID=159). You can select one of the usual specializations or the auspice specialization.

 Auspice mounts gain the following benefits: Your companion is marked by your deity's religious symbol as a sacred creature of your deity. Its proficiency rank in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) increases to expert, it can speak the language associated with your deity's servitors ([Celestial](/Traits.aspx?ID=23) for champions who follow the tenets of good), and its Intelligence modifier increases by 2 and its Wisdom modifier by 1.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 98 **Prerequisites** [Imposing Destrier](/Feats.aspx?ID=5908) --- Guided by your ongoing care, your steed has developed incredible intelligence and skill. The mount you gained with Faithful Steed is now a [specialized animal companion](/Companions.aspx?Type=Specialized). You can select one of the usual specializations or the auspice specialization. A faithful steed with the auspice specialization gains the following benefits.
  • It gains the [celestial](/Traits.aspx?ID=551), [fiend](/Traits.aspx?ID=600), or [monitor](/Traits.aspx?ID=655) trait—whichever best matches your deity's servitors, and its appearance shifts to look more like those servitors. It also gains the [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) trait if it's a celestial or the [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521) trait if it's a fiend.
  • Its Intelligence modifier increases by 2 and its Wisdom modifier by 1.
  • Its proficiency rank in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) increases to expert.
  • It can speak the language associated with your deity's servitors (such as [Empyrean](/Languages.aspx?ID=115) for celestials, [Chthonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=114) for demons, or [Requian](/Languages.aspx?ID=34) for psychopomps).
  • Its maximum Hit Points increase by 20, increasing to 25 at 18th level and 30 at 20th level. If the mount has the celestial trait, the extra HP increase by 5, and the mount gains weakness 5 to unholy. If it has the fiend trait, the extra HP increase by 5, and the mount gains weakness 5 to holy.
  • It gains wings that grant it a fly Speed equal to its land Speed.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 252

**Prerequisites**
expert in a skill with the [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) action; [Assurance](/Feats.aspx?ID=756) in that skill

</column>

---

You know basic facts off the top of your head. Choose a skill you’re an expert in that has the Recall Knowledge action and for which you have the Assurance feat. You can use the Recall Knowledge action with that skill as a free action once per round. If you do, you must use Assurance on the skill check.

**Special** You can select this feat multiple times, choosing a different skill each time. You can use Automatic Knowledge with any skills you have chosen, but you can still use Automatic Knowledge only once per round.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Exploration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=66" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 78

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11)

</column>

---

When confronted with the unknown, you can receive knowledge beyond your own experience via written messages delivered by your hand. You spend 10 minutes seated while holding a writing utensil, using it to make small circular motions as you open your mind to the forces around you. You receive information as your hand writes on its own, guided by spirits. At the end of these 10 minutes, [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) with any [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) skill in which you are not trained, using your Occultism modifier instead of your modifier with that skill. The strain of this spirit channeling leaves you [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) for the next 10 minutes.

fields.text: Feat 2 Automatic Writing Uncommon Concentrate Exploration General Skill Source Dark Archive (Remastered) pg. 78 Frequency once per day Prerequisites Expert in Occultism When confronted with the unknown, you can receive knowledge beyond your own experience via written messages delivered by your hand. You spend 10 minutes seated while holding a writing utensil, using it to make small circular motions as you open your mind to the forces around you. You receive information as your hand writes on its own, guided by spirits. At the end of these 10 minutes, Recall Knowledge with any Lore skill in which you are not trained, using your Occultism modifier instead of your modifier with that skill. The strain of this spirit channeling leaves you stupefied 1 for the next 10 minutes.

[Automaton Armament](/Feats.aspx?ID=3090) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Automaton" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=398" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 39

</column>

---

You've been provided a body part designed for combat. You gain either a claw or pincer unarmed attack. The claw deals 1d4 slashing damage, is in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group, and has the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), and [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) traits. The pincer deals 1d6 piercing damage, is in the brawling group, and has the [grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=35) and unarmed traits.

 Your body can be reconfigured; you can select this feat at any level, and you can retrain into or out of this feat or change the type of attack you gain.

**Enhancement** Your attacking part is reinforced. Increase the damage die of the unarmed attack you gain from this feat by one step (from 1d4 to 1d6, or from 1d6 to 1d8).

You have come to better understand the process that made your body and the magic that powers it. You gain the trained proficiency rank in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) and [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4). If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You also gain the [Additional Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=5114) feat for [Automaton Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41).

**Enhancement** Increase your proficiency rank in your choice of either Arcana or Crafting to expert.

If your weapon doesn’t possess it already, it gains the effects of the [animated](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2831) property rune. <title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Avatar's Audience](/Feats.aspx?ID=308) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Cleric" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=26" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 127

</column>

---

Your extensive service has made you a lesser herald of your deity, which affords you certain privileges. First, any creature you encounter knows instinctively that you speak for your deity. Second, if you conduct the [commune](/Rituals.aspx?ID=6) ritual to contact your deity, you don’t have to pay any cost and you automatically get a critical success. Third, once per day, you can cast [_plane shift_](/Spells.aspx?ID=222) as a divine innate spell, but only to travel to the realm of your deity. When you cast it this way, its casting time is 1 minute, your religious symbol is a sufficient tuning fork for this spell, and you appear exactly where you want to be. If you’re in your deity’s realm due to this spell, you can return to the point you left when you cast it by spending a single action, which has the concentrate and divine traits.

Your training regimen has given you particular advantages when it comes to enforcing the interests of your faith. You gain a +1 status bonus to saving throws against [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579) spells and effects that deal [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage. You can use [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) to [Coerce](/Actions.aspx?ID=2394), [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=2391), or [Track](/Actions.aspx?ID=2408) as long as you are in a town or city with a church dedicated to your deity, extracting clues from the faithful with displays of your piety.

    level="1"

    pfs=""
>
[Avenger of Envy](/Feats.aspx?ID=9411) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Revenge of the Runelords</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #220: Crypt of Runes](/Sources.aspx?ID=284) pg. 84

</column>

---

You've become the champion of the runelords of envy. Their support gives you a heightened awareness of your own failings, but you can call their spirits to your side to protect you from harm. The first time each day you critically fail a skill check or saving throw, you gain 1 Mythic Point. You gain the Aegis of Envy activity.

**Activate—Aegis of Envy** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561));  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Spend 1 Mythic Point. The spirits of eight runelords of envy (Naaft, Tannaris, Ivamura, Jurah, Chalsardra, Esedrea, Zarve, Desamelia, and Phirandi) swirl about you for 1 minute. While at least one of the spirits remains, whenever you take damage, you can use a reaction that has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait to gain resistance 10 to that damage, or resistance 20 if the damage was dealt by Xanderghul, the runelord of pride. Each time you use this feat to gain resistance, one of the spirits disappears.

<title level="2">Vengeance Feats</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #220: Crypt of Runes](/Sources.aspx?ID=284) pg. 84

During Chapter 2 of this adventure, the PCs can take on the vengeful mantle of a specific runelord's vengeance and embody that need to avenge the violations Runelord Xanderghul has inflicted upon their legacies by creating risen runelords. These rewards manifest in the form of a bonus feat, chosen from the following. A PC can only select one vengeance feat. If you wish to use these feats in the context of another campaign, a mythic PC should be required to use one of their mythic feat slots granted from their mythic destiny.

**Related Feats**: [Avenger of Gluttony](/Feats.aspx?ID=9412), [Avenger of Greed](/Feats.aspx?ID=9413), [Avenger of Lust](/Feats.aspx?ID=9414), [Avenger of Sloth](/Feats.aspx?ID=9415), [Avenger of Wrath](/Feats.aspx?ID=9416)

>
[Avenger of Gluttony](/Feats.aspx?ID=9412) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Revenge of the Runelords</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #220: Crypt of Runes](/Sources.aspx?ID=284) pg. 84

</column>

---

You've become the champion of the runelords of gluttony, and their hungry spirits are always near you. Whenever a spell or other magical effect restores Hit Points to you, you can choose to reduce the number of Hit Points you regain by any amount. The first time each day you reduce the Hit Points by an amount  equal to your level, you gain 1 Mythic Point. You gain the Gluttonous Feast activity.

**Activate—Gluttonous Feast** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561));  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Spend 1 Mythic Point. The spirits of four runelords of gluttony (Kaliphesta, Atharend, Aethusa, and Goparlis) briefly appear in spaces within 60 feet of you. Each living creature adjacent to at least one of the spirits takes 4d6 void damage per adjacent spirit, to a maximum of 16d6 void damage if they are adjacent to all four spirits. Each target receives a basic Fortitude save against the damage, against the higher of your class DC or spell DC, but Xanderghul, the Runelord of Pride, treats the result of his saving throw as one degree of success worse.

 You gain temporary Hit Points equal to half the damage a single creature takes from this effect; calculate these temporary Hit Points using the creature that took the most damage. These temporary Hit Points last 1 minute.

**Source** [Pathfinder #220: Crypt of Runes](/Sources.aspx?ID=284) pg. 84

During Chapter 2 of this adventure, the PCs can take on the vengeful mantle of a specific runelord's vengeance and embody that need to avenge the violations Runelord Xanderghul has inflicted upon their legacies by creating risen runelords. These rewards manifest in the form of a bonus feat, chosen from the following. A PC can only select one vengeance feat. If you wish to use these feats in the context of another campaign, a mythic PC should be required to use one of their mythic feat slots granted from their mythic destiny.

**Related Feats**: [Avenger of Envy](/Feats.aspx?ID=9411), [Avenger of Greed](/Feats.aspx?ID=9413), [Avenger of Lust](/Feats.aspx?ID=9414), [Avenger of Sloth](/Feats.aspx?ID=9415), [Avenger of Wrath](/Feats.aspx?ID=9416)

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Revenge of the Runelords</spoilers>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #220: Crypt of Runes](/Sources.aspx?ID=284) pg. 84

</column>

---

You've become a champion of the runelords of greed. Their whispers encourage you to prepare for disasters that might never come to pass. The first time each day you touch an object worth at least 2,000 gp that you've never touched before, you gain 1 Mythic Point. You gain the Convocation of Greed activity.

**Activate—Convocation of Greed** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561));  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Spend 1 Mythic Point. The spirits of the eight runelords of greed (Kaladurnae, Fethryr, Gimmel, Ligniya, Mazmiranna, Aethusa, Haphrama, and Karzoug) appear and bolster the armaments of you and your companions. For each of the spirits, one creature of your choice within 60 feet gains a +2 item bonus to AC, attack rolls, or saving throws (chosen by the creature) for 1 minute. These bonuses increase to +4 while the creature is within 100 feet of Xanderghul, the Runelord of Pride. A creature can receive bonuses from multiple runelords at once (gaining bonuses to both AC and attack rolls, for example), but the bonuses aren't cumulative.

**Source** [Pathfinder #220: Crypt of Runes](/Sources.aspx?ID=284) pg. 84

These rewards manifest in the form of a bonus feat, chosen from the following. A PC can only select one vengeance feat. If you wish to use these feats in the context of another campaign, a mythic PC should be required to use one of their mythic feat slots granted from their mythic destiny.

---

You've become a champion of the runelords of sloth. They spur you toward idleness, and their spirits are slow to come to your aid. Once they arrive, however, their combined might is undeniable. The first time each day you spend 10 minutes resting, you gain 1 Mythic Point. During this time, you don't need to sleep, but you can't perform activities like [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=2621) or [Treat Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=2399). You gain the Summon Sloth activity.

**Activate—Summon Sloth** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561));  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Spend 1 Mythic Point. You summon the spirit of one of the seven runelords of sloth (Xirie, Ilthyrius, Azeradni, Zalelet, Krenlith, Ivarinna, or Krune) into an unoccupied space within 30 feet. Allies can move through a space occupied by one of these spirits, but a spirit's space is [greater difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) for your enemies.

 For the next minute, you can use a two-action activity with the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait to summon another runelord spirit in a different space within 30 feet, to a maximum of seven spirits. While you are within 120 feet of Xanderghul, the Runelord of Pride, you can summon an additional spirit as a single action (instead of as a two-action activity). At the end of the each of your turns, each spirit fires arcane energy at a different enemy of your choice within 120 feet of it (or does nothing if no enemy is within range), dealing 2d4+2 force damage. After 1 minute, all spirits disappear.

<title level="2">Vengeance Feats</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #220: Crypt of Runes](/Sources.aspx?ID=284) pg. 84

During Chapter 2 of this adventure, the PCs can take on the vengeful mantle of a specific runelord's vengeance and embody that need to avenge the violations Runelord Xanderghul has inflicted upon their legacies by creating risen runelords. These rewards manifest in the form of a bonus feat, chosen from the following. A PC can only select one vengeance feat. If you wish to use these feats in the context of another campaign, a mythic PC should be required to use one of their mythic feat slots granted from their mythic destiny.

**Related Feats**: [Avenger of Envy](/Feats.aspx?ID=9411), [Avenger of Gluttony](/Feats.aspx?ID=9412), [Avenger of Greed](/Feats.aspx?ID=9413), [Avenger of Lust](/Feats.aspx?ID=9414), [Avenger of Wrath](/Feats.aspx?ID=9416)
