>
[Bloc Tactics](/Feats.aspx?ID=7358) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 123

**Archetype** [Broken Chain](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=291)

**Prerequisites**
[Broken Chain Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7357)

</column>

---

You have experience in undertaking direct action and know how to protect the identity and health of you and your allies when doing so. During your [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575), you can select a number of targets equal to half your level. You disguise the targets to hide their identities, which gives them a +4 status bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks to prevent others from seeing through their disguises, and lets them add their level even if untrained. Additionally, the disguises also protect from smoke, fumes, and inhaled substances, giving the targets a +3 status bonus to saving throws against them. The targets can quickly doff or don their disguises with a two-action activity.

</title>

<traits>

**Prerequisites**
[Divine Dragonblood](/Feats.aspx?ID=5727)

</column>

---

Your connection to the divine has sanctified your blood, but the power only manifests when you are shedding it. Choose [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) or [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521). While you are taking [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86), you can [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) to coat a piercing or slashing weapon you’re wielding with your blood. Until the end of your turn, your Strikes with that weapon deal an additional 1d6 [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage with the chosen trait to creatures with the opposing trait. Alternatively, you can deal 1d6 slashing damage to yourself (which can’t be resisted in any way) as part of that Interact action if you aren’t taking persistent bleed damage.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Blood Component Substitution](/Feats.aspx?ID=1824) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Sorcerer" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=148" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 140

</column>

---

You can bypass the need for incantations and gestures by drawing energy directly from your blood, causing you to visibly glow the color of your blood and crackle with magical energy. When you Cast a Spell, you can replace all verbal, material, or somatic spellcasting components with a blood component. To use a blood component, you lose Hit Points equal to twice the spell's level as the energy in your blood is depleted, and you can't decrease the Hit Points lost in any way. As usual for altering components, this has no effect on the number of actions required to Cast the Spell, and your Cast a Spell activity gains the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait but not the [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104) trait. You can't use blood components to replace any required part of a spell's cost.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Eidolon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=386" />
<trait label="Evolution" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=394" />
<trait label="Summoner" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=392" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 69

**Prerequisites**
[Bloodletting Claws](/Feats.aspx?ID=2900)

**Requirements**
Your eidolon's last action dealt bleed damage to a living creature.

</column>

---

Your eidolon flies into a frenzy. It gains the benefits of [_boost eidolon_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1045) and gains temporary HP equal to your level, but takes a –2 penalty to AC. It can't voluntarily end the frenzy or start another frenzy while in the frenzy. The frenzy lasts for 1 minute, after which your eidolon is [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=15) for 1 minute and can't start another frenzy for 1 minute.

You use the lifeblood of your enemies to heal your allies. You pool the blood of the creature on the ground in a space adjacent to the triggering creature, infusing it with healing properties. <title level="2">Paragons of Promise</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #150: Broken Promises](/Sources.aspx?ID=15) pg. 75

The citizens of Promise represent some of the most capable experts, greatest minds, and powerful warriors on Golarion—ideal teachers and trainers for PCs who want to maximize their own potential. If the PCs secure Visitor’s Pins or an alliance with Mengkare, their access to Promise’s trainers and records unlock all of the following uncommon class feats.

**Related Feats**: [Apex Companion](/Feats.aspx?ID=1160), [Aura of Unbreakable Virtue](/Feats.aspx?ID=1161), [Efficient Alchemy (Paragon)](/Feats.aspx?ID=1163), [Emblazon Divinity](/Feats.aspx?ID=1164), [Enduring Debilitation](/Feats.aspx?ID=1165), [Golden Body](/Feats.aspx?ID=1166), [Song of the Fallen](/Feats.aspx?ID=1168), [Spell Mastery](/Feats.aspx?ID=1843), [Superior Sight](/Feats.aspx?ID=1170), [Ultimate Flexibility](/Feats.aspx?ID=1732), [Unstoppable Juggernaut](/Feats.aspx?ID=1631)

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 141 **Prerequisites** a bloodline based on a specific type of creature --- You permanently mutate to become more like the creatures of your bloodline. You gain the appropriate trait or traits for those types of creatures ([aberration](/Traits.aspx?ID=1) for [aberrant](/Bloodlines.aspx?ID=1), [angel](/Traits.aspx?ID=8) and [celestial](/Traits.aspx?ID=23) for [angelic](/Bloodlines.aspx?ID=2), [psychopomp](/Traits.aspx?ID=232) and [monitor](/Traits.aspx?ID=111) for [psychopomp](/Bloodlines.aspx?ID=13), and so on). You gain [low-light vision](/Rules.aspx?ID=416) or [darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=415), if one is appropriate for creatures with those traits. Choose one of the following.
  • If the creatures associated with your bloodline have the ability to fly, you gain a fly Speed equal to your land Speed.
  • If the creatures associated with your bloodline are [aquatic](/Traits.aspx?ID=168) or [amphibious](/Traits.aspx?ID=207), you become amphibious, able to breathe water and air equally well, and you gain a swim Speed equal to your Speed.
  • If creatures associated with your bloodline have a resistance or immunity to acid, cold, electricity, fire, negative, or sonic, choose an energy type your bloodline is immune or resistant to and gain resistance 20 against that energy type.

[Bloodrager Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7239) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Class" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=397" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 60

**Archetype** [Bloodrager](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=283)

**Prerequisites**
[Bloodrager](/Instincts.aspx?ID=14)

</column>

---

Drinking powerful blood has awakened magical potential within you. You gain a spell repertoire with two cantrips of your choice, from either the [arcane](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=1) or [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) spell list. You choose these cantrips from the common spells for your tradition or from other spells you have access to on that tradition’s spell list. At least one cantrip must require a spell attack roll. You’re trained in spell attack modifier and spell DC. Your key spellcasting attribute for these spells is Charisma. Spells in your repertoire gain the [rage](/Traits.aspx?ID=680) trait while you are [raging](/Actions.aspx?ID=2802), and when you [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) from your repertoire, you become [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) 1 (or increase the value of your drained condition by 1); you can reduce the value of this condition only by Harvesting Blood. 

You become trained in Arcana if you chose arcane cantrips or Religion if you chose divine cantrips. If you were already trained in this skill, you become trained in a skill of your choice. You also gain the Harvest Blood action. 

<document level="2" id="action-3065" />

<title level="2">Bloodrager Dedication leads to...</title>
[Blood Calls Blood](/Feats.aspx?ID=7240), [Hematocritical](/Feats.aspx?ID=7244), [Rising Blood Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=7241), [Siphon Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=7242)

---

You’re extraordinarily sensitive to the presence of blood. You gain bloodsense as an [imprecise sense](/Rules.aspx?ID=2407) with a range of 15 feet. This allows you to sense the presence of creatures, living or dead, that have blood (this includes most creatures that aren’t immune to bleed). You’re similarly able to detect the presence of fresh blood in volumes of one pint or more, so long as it’s no more than 24 hours old.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Incapacitation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=631" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=647" />
<trait label="Visual" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=727" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 47

**Archetype** [Dandy](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=246)

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Dandy Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6302)

**Trigger**
You’re about to roll initiative.

</column>

---

In socially exclusive venues like the Ivy District's Bloom Cabaret, you've learned how to make an entrance. This confidence doesn't betray you when you find yourself about to enter combat, allowing you to throw enemies temporarily off-balance. Once per day, you can choose to not roll initiative. Instead, you voluntarily go last. If more than one character uses this ability or another ability to go last, use the normal rules for resolving a tie: NPCs and monsters act before PCs, and within those groups, the creature can choose whichever order they want.

 Enemies who can see you must attempt a Will saving throw against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. On a failure, the enemy is overcome with anticipation for what you'll do or say next and can't use reactions for 1 round.

 In addition, during your first turn, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to the first Deception, Diplomacy, or Intimidation check you attempt.

</column>

---

You can capably deliver toxins with a [blowgun](/Weapons.aspx?ID=424). Your blowgun [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) can apply [injury](/Traits.aspx?ID=635) [poisons](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) even if they deal no damage due to a creature's resistance. If you critically succeed at a blowgun Strike using a poisoned dart, the target's initial save against the poison is one degree of success worse than the creature rolls; this is a [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654) effect.

 In addition, if you make a blowgun Strike while [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=96), you don't automatically become [observed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=84). Instead, immediately attempt a [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) check against the Perception DC of the target. If you succeed, you don't become observed, and are hidden (if you were undetected, you still become hidden rather than remaining undetected).

>
[Boaster's Challenge](/Feats.aspx?ID=1068) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=106" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 74

**Archetype** [Firebrand Braggart](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=24)

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5), Expert in [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6), or Expert in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7); [Firebrand Braggart Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1067)

</column>

---

You call out a foe, causing them to become flustered and easier to defeat. Select one creature you can see and declare a challenge. For your challenge, attempt a Deception, Diplomacy, or Intimidation check against that creature’s Will DC. Your challenge must include a [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=101), [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), or [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163) component and gains the corresponding trait. If you succeed, you gain a +2 status bonus to damage rolls with your weapon or unarmed Strikes against that foe until the end of your next turn; if you have master proficiency in the skill you used, you gain a +4 status bonus instead, and if you’re legendary, you gain a +6 status bonus. On a critical success, the status bonus lasts for 3 rounds instead. Whether you succeed or fail, creatures who witnessed your challenge gain a +4 circumstance bonus to their Will DCs against your attempts to challenge for 1 minute.

<title level="2">Boaster's Challenge leads to...</title>
[Demanding Challenge](/Feats.aspx?ID=1073)

    right="Feat 9"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Bodily Disintegration](/Feats.aspx?ID=9404) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Automaton" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=398" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 111

**Frequency**
once per hour

</column>

---

You have such complete control of your component atoms that you can momentarily separate them far enough apart for you to pass through solid material. You focus on your physical body and will the parts of it to disassemble momentarily. You Stride. You can pass through creatures and tiny cracks during this movement. You cannot pass through solid walls or magical boundaries such as a [_wall of force_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1749). If you haven’t completely passed through a creature or object by the end of your movement, you take 4d6 bludgeoning damage and are shunted to the nearest spot that you can occupy.

**Enhancement** When you use Bodily Disintegration, you can move through solid walls and delay fully reassembling your body, causing you to become [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) until the start of your next turn.

</title>

 You can use Body of Air as a reaction only when the trigger is met, but you can use it as a 2-action activity without the trigger being met.

---

>
[Bodysnatcher](/Feats.aspx?ID=3892) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Blood Lords</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Polymorph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=127" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #184: The Ghouls Hunger](/Sources.aspx?ID=147) pg. 80

**Archetype** [Ghoul](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=178)

**Prerequisites**
[Secret Eater](/Feats.aspx?ID=3890)

</column>

---

Your secret-stealing maggots reveal how to devour more than just the flesh and secrets of a victim; you can ingest and assume their whole physical appearance. When you [Consume Flesh](/Feats.aspx?ID=3504) of a creature of your size or smaller, you can assume the physical form of the creature immediately after becoming satiated or fully satiated. Using Bodysnatcher counts as creating a disguise for the [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) use of [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5). Your transformation automatically defeats Perception DCs to determine you are a member of the ancestry or creature type into which you transformed, and you gain a +4 circumstance bonus to your Deception DC to prevent others from seeing through your disguise. You do not gain the special abilities, skills, voice, memories, or other characteristics of the creature you consumed, only their physical form. Unlike [Change Shape](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=8), Bodysnatcher can be used to gain the appearance of a specific individual whose flesh you've consumed. This effect lasts until you are no longer satiated and can only be used once per individual creature.

fields.text: Feat 14 Bodysnatcher May contain spoilers from Blood Lords Rare Archetype Divine Polymorph Transmutation Source Pathfinder #184: The Ghouls Hunger pg. 80 Archetype Ghoul Prerequisites Secret Eater Your secret-stealing maggots reveal how to devour more than just the flesh and secrets of a victim; you can ingest and assume their whole physical appearance. When you Consume Flesh of a creature of your size or smaller, you can assume the physical form of the creature immediately after becoming satiated or fully satiated. Using Bodysnatcher counts as creating a disguise for the Impersonate use of Deception. Your transformation automatically defeats Perception DCs to determine you are a member of the ancestry or creature type into which you transformed, and you gain a +4 circumstance bonus to your Deception DC to prevent others from seeing through your disguise. You do not gain the special abilities, skills, voice, memories, or other characteristics of the creature you consumed, only their physical form. Unlike Change Shape, Bodysnatcher can be used to gain the appearance of a specific individual whose flesh you've consumed. This effect lasts until you are no longer satiated and can only be used once per individual creature.

<trait label="Metamagic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=107" />
<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=166" />

**Prerequisites**
[arcane bond](/Classes.aspx?ID=12)

**Requirements**
The last action you used was Drain Bonded Item.

</column>

---

By carefully manipulating the arcane energies stored in your bonded item as you drain it, you can conserve just enough power to cast another, slightly weaker spell. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell using the energy from Drain Bonded Item, you gain an extra use of Drain Bonded Item.     right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Bonded Animal](/Feats.aspx?ID=5127) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Downtime" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=49" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 253

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)

</column>

---

You forge strong connections with animals. You can spend 7 days of downtime regularly interacting with a normal animal (not a companion or other special animal) that is friendly or helpful to you. After this duration, attempt a [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) check against the animal's Will DC. If successful, you bond with the animal. The animal is permanently bonded to you until you form a bond with a different animal or do something egregious to break your bond.

A helpful animal is easier to [direct](/Actions.aspx?ID=2400). If your bonded animal is level –1, it gains the [minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=653) trait, allowing you to command it more efficiently. The maximum level of creature that can be your minion increases to 3 if you're a master in Nature and to 11 if you're legendary.

**Special** You can’t have both a bonded animal and an animal companion (though you can have both a bonded animal and a pet or familiar).

<title level="2">Bonded Animal leads to...</title>
[Ferocious Beasts](/Feats.aspx?ID=4527)
